title: The Standard Conjectures on Algebraic Cycles

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over a field, and use a Weil cohomology theory with its cycle-class map. The standard conjectures ask that the cohomological operators and relations dictated by algebraic cycles actually have algebraic realizations. In particular, are the inverse hard-Lefschetz operators induced by algebraic correspondences, and are the K\"unneth projectors onto the individual cohomological degrees algebraic? The collection also includes the agreement of numerical and homological equivalence and the positivity assertion for primitive algebraic classes.

title: The Abundance Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $X$ be a projective minimal model with nonnegative Kodaira dimension and nef canonical divisor $K_X$. Is $K_X$ semiample, meaning that a positive integral multiple of it is base-point-free?

title: Hilbert's 16th Problem: Topology of Algebraic Curves and Limit Cycles

category.name: geometry

statement: Determine the topology of real algebraic curves and the maximum number of polynomial-flow limit cycles at each fixed degree.

title: Sofic Groups

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Is every group sofic? Here soficity means that every finite subset admits arbitrarily accurate approximations by permutations of a finite set: multiplication is respected on all but a prescribed small proportion of points, and distinct group elements are represented by permutations differing on nearly all points.

title: The Tate Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $X$ be smooth and projective over a finite field, let $r\geq0$, and let $\ell$ differ from the field characteristic. Must every Frobenius-invariant class in $H^{2r}_{\mathrm{et}}(X_{\overline{\mathbb F}_q},\mathbb Q_\ell(r))$ be a $\mathbb Q_\ell$-linear combination of cycle classes of codimension-$r$ algebraic cycles defined over the finite field? Applying the assertion after finite field extensions gives the usual Tate-class formulation.

title: Serre's Positivity Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement:
Let $R$ be a regular local ring and $P,Q$ prime ideals for which $R/(P+Q)$ has finite length and $\dim(R/P)+\dim(R/Q)=\dim R$. Must Serre's intersection multiplicity
\[\chi^R(R/P,R/Q)=\sum_{i\geq0}(-1)^i\operatorname{length}_R\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/P,R/Q)\]
be strictly positive?

title: The Sofic Groups Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Is every countable discrete group sofic? For each finite collection of elements and each positive error tolerance, one requires permutations of a finite set that almost preserve the specified products in normalized Hamming distance and almost separate every pair of distinct specified elements.

title: Arthur's Conjectures

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For a connected reductive group over a global field, describe the constituents and multiplicities of the discrete automorphic spectrum by global Arthur parameters. The desired description must agree with the local parameterizations at each place and with the associated automorphic $L$-functions.

title: The Cartan-Hadamard Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement:
A Cartan--Hadamard manifold is complete, simply connected, and has nonpositive sectional curvature. In dimension $n$, must every bounded sufficiently regular domain $\Omega$ in such a manifold satisfy the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric bound
\[|\partial\Omega|\geq n\omega_n^{1/n}|\Omega|^{(n-1)/n},\]
where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball?

title: The Heilbronn Triangle Problem

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For an $n$-point subset $P$ of the unit square, take the least area of a triangle with three distinct vertices in $P$. Determine the supremum of this least area over all choices of $P$, including its asymptotic order as $n$ grows.

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For a number field $K$, does an algorithm exist that takes an arbitrary multivariable polynomial with coefficients in $K$ and decides whether it has a zero in $K$? Determine for which number fields such a decision procedure exists. Solutions are sought in the field $K$ itself.

title: Borsuk's Conjecture

category.name: geometry

statement: For every $n\geq1$, can each bounded subset of $\mathbb R^n$ with positive diameter be partitioned into at most $n+1$ subsets whose diameters are all strictly smaller than that of the original set?

title: Erdős Conjecture on Arithmetic Progressions

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ satisfy $\sum_{a\in A}1/a=\infty$. Must $A$ contain arithmetic progressions of every finite length? The progression must have positive common difference.

title: Grand Riemann Hypothesis

category.name: number_theory

statement: For every automorphic $L$-function in the standard unitary normalization, must every nontrivial zero have real part $1/2$? Zeros forced by the archimedean factors are excluded from the nontrivial zeros.

title: Crouzeix's Conjecture

category.name: algebra

statement: Does the numerical range control every analytic matrix function with universal constant two?

title: Borel Conjecture

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For every $n\geq2$, must every subset of $\mathbb R^n$ containing a unit segment in each direction have both Hausdorff dimension and Minkowski dimension equal to $n$?

title: Birkhoff Conjecture

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: In a smooth strictly convex planar billiard table, particles move along straight lines and reflect with equal incidence and reflection angles. If the billiard dynamics is completely integrable, must the boundary of the table be an ellipse?

title: Abundance Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry

category.name: geometry

statement: Among configurations of $n$ distinct points in the unit square, maximize the area of the smallest triangle formed by three of the points. Determine the optimal value or its asymptotic size.

title: Kirby Problem 1.12

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For a knot in an oriented three-manifold, Dehn filling along a slope on its peripheral torus produces a closed three-manifold. Two fillings are purely cosmetic if their resulting manifolds are orientation-preservingly homeomorphic; they are chirally cosmetic if an orientation-reversing homeomorphism identifies the results. The question has four parts. Can inequivalent slopes ever be purely cosmetic? If two knots in a closed oriented three-manifold have orientation-preservingly homeomorphic complements, must an ambient homeomorphism carry one knot to the other? Does every nontrivial knot in $S^3$ admit no purely cosmetic pair? Finally, must a knot in $S^3$ other than a torus knot $T_{2g+1,2}$ admit no chirally cosmetic pair of inequivalent slopes?

title: Kirby Problem 3.24

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Suppose a word-hyperbolic group has Gromov boundary homeomorphic to $S^2$. Must it act as a cocompact Kleinian group? More generally, if its boundary is planar, must a finite-index subgroup be a convex-cocompact Kleinian group? A Kleinian group is a discrete group of isometries of hyperbolic three-space.

title: Kirby Problem 4.46

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Is every group good in the sense of four-dimensional topological surgery? Goodness is the group-theoretic condition that permits the disk-embedding theorem with that fundamental group: algebraically suitable immersed disks in a topological four-manifold can be replaced by embedded disks with the required boundaries and dual spheres. The question quantifies over all groups, rather than only groups of a given growth type.

title: Kirby Problem 5.3

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: The Hilbert--Smith assertion asks whether every locally compact group acting faithfully and continuously on a connected manifold is a Lie group. The companion question concerns an action of a Cantor group on a Euclidean neighborhood retract: must the subset $A$ of points with trivial stabilizer be a homology-$Z$-subset? This homological negligibility means that $H_*(U,U\setminus A;\mathbb Z)=0$ for every open subset $U$ of the ambient neighborhood retract.

title: Decomposing an eulerian graph into cycles.

category.name: graph_theory

statement: Conjecture Every simple eulerian graph on $n$ vertices can be decomposed into at most $\frac{1}{2}(n-1)$ cycles.

title: List Hadwiger Conjecture

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Conjecture Every $K_t$-minor-free graph is $c t$-list-colourable for some constant $c\geq1$.

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Suppose $G$ admits a finite $K(G,1)$. If $G$ does not contain any Baumslag-Solitar subgroups $BS(m,n)$, is $G$ necessarily hyperbolic? If $G$ embeds in a hyperbolic group, is it hyperbolic?

title: Zariski–Lipman conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Let $V$ be a complex algebraic variety with coordinate ring $R$. If the module of derivations of $R$ is free over $R$, must $V$ be smooth?

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.13

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For $P(z)=\sum_{k=1}^n\varepsilon_kz^k$ with $\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$, is there an absolute $A>0$ such that
\[\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|>(1+A)\sqrt n\]
for all such polynomials? This asks for a uniform gap above the square-root scale.

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.14

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For every $n$, can one choose coefficients $\varepsilon_k\in\{-1,1\}$ so that $P(z)=\sum_{k=1}^n\varepsilon_kz^k$ satisfies $\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|>C_2\sqrt n$ for an absolute $C_2>0$? The stronger version asks for such a lower bound together with an upper bound $\max_{|z|=1}|P(z)|<C_1\sqrt n$ with an absolute $C_1$.

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.31

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Consider $f(z)=\sum_{k=0}^na_kz^k$ with $|a_k|=1$. The problem asks about uniform flatness on the unit circle, including whether the upper bound $\sqrt n+O(n^{3/10+\varepsilon})$ can be sharpened to $\sqrt n+O(n^\varepsilon)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. It also asks whether the minimum modulus can exceed $(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt n$ for sufficiently large $n$, whether both minimum and maximum can lie between $(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt n$ and $(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt n$, and whether an $O(1)$ error can replace those relative errors. Further versions ask for a uniform gap above $\sqrt n$ when the coefficients are signs, either at consecutive exponents or at arbitrary distinct positive integer exponents.

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.94

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C$ be simply connected with at least two boundary points, and let $\phi:\Omega\to\mathbb D$ be a conformal bijection. Determine the exponents $p$ for which
\[\int_\Omega|\phi'(z)|^p\,dA(z)<\infty\]
holds for every such domain. In particular, is the universal sharp range $4/3<p<4$?

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.96

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For a conformal map $f:\mathbb D\to\mathbb D$, let its integral-means exponent be
\[\beta_f(p)=\limsup_{r\uparrow1}\frac{\log\int_0^{2\pi}|f'(re^{i\theta})|^p\,d\theta}{\log(1/(1-r))},\qquad B(p)=\sup_f\beta_f(p).\]
Is the universal spectrum equal to $-p-1$ for $p\leq-2$, to $p^2/4$ for $-2\leq p\leq2$, and to $p-1$ for $p\geq2$?

title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.109

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For an analytic univalent $f$ in the unit disk and $\lambda>0$, set
\[I_{-\lambda}(r,f')=\left(\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|f'(re^{i\theta})|^{-\lambda}\,d\theta\right)^{1/\lambda}.\]
Determine the maximal growth rate as $r\uparrow1$. In particular, for $\lambda=2$, must it be $O((1-r)^{-1/2})$, the rate of the Koebe function?

title: Flint Hills series

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Does the Flint Hills series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 1/(n^3\sin^2 n)$ converge?

title: Vlasov–Maxwell regularity

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Establish global regularity, or exhibit breakdown, for solutions of the Vlasov–Maxwell equations from appropriate smooth initial data.

title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Mutually Unbiased Bases

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: In $\mathbb C^6$, two orthonormal bases are mutually unbiased if the absolute value of every cross-basis inner product is $1/\sqrt6$. What is the largest number of bases that are pairwise mutually unbiased?

title: 10 Lectures and 42 Open Problems — Detection Threshold for SBM for three of more communities

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: What is the partial recovery threshold for the Stochastic Block Model on $k\geq 3$ communities.

title: How many colors is it necessary to use so that, if you paint every single point of the two-dimensional plane some color

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Determine the least number of colors for a coloring of all points of $\mathbb R^2$ in which points at distance one have different colors. For the closed disk $B_r(0)$, determine the corresponding chromatic number as a function of $r$. In particular, at what radius does it first reach four?

title: A set of points S is Euclidean Ramsey if, for every k, there exists an N so that every k-coloring of Euclidean N-space c

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Call a finite point set $S$ Euclidean Ramsey if, for every finite number of colors, some Euclidean dimension has the property that every coloring of the whole space contains a monochromatic isometric copy of $S$. Must every finite set that lies on a sphere be Euclidean Ramsey? The four-point subsets of a circle are included.

title: Suppose I have a sequence of positive integers whose reciprocals sum to infinity

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: If $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ has divergent reciprocal sum, must it contain arithmetic progressions of arbitrarily large finite length with positive common difference?

title: Exact van der Waerden numbers

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every coloring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $r$ colors contains a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length $k$. Determine the unknown exact values of $W(r,k)$.

title: Chromatic number of the plane

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Determine the least number of colors needed to color the Euclidean plane so that points at unit distance receive different colors.

title: Arnold and Arnold–Givental conjectures

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: For a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed symplectic manifold, prove the Arnold lower bound on its number of fixed points in terms of Morse-theoretic data. In the Lagrangian Arnold–Givental form, prove the corresponding lower bound for intersections of a Lagrangian submanifold with its Hamiltonian image under the standard hypotheses.

title: Banach's simple Lebesgue spectrum problem

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Does there exist an ergodic measure-preserving transformation whose Koopman operator has simple Lebesgue spectrum?

title: Rokhlin multiple-mixing problem

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Is every strongly mixing measure-preserving transformation strongly mixing of order three?

title: Distances among Point Sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: For a point set $P$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, let $f_d(P)$ be the number of unit-distance point pairs: $$f_d(P) = \left| \{ (u,v) \mid u, v \in P, \, \|u-v\| = 1 \} \right| \;;$$ and let $f_d(n)$ be the maximum over all sets of $n$ points: $$f_d(n) = \max_{|P| = n} f_d(P) \;.$$ Further, let $g_d(P)$ denote the number of distinct distances induced by a set of points $P$: $$g_d(P) = \left| \{ \|u-v\| \mid u, v \in P \} \right| \;;$$ and let $g_d(n)$ be the minimum over all sets of $n$ points: $$g_d(n) = \min_{|P|=n} g_d(P) \;.$$ Give upper and lower bounds on $f_d(n)$ and $g_d(n)$, particularly for $d=2$ and $d=3$.

title: Scalar Curvature Question [?12]: Q-Non-Essentiality of Manifolds with Sc > 0

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian manifold of strictly positive scalar curvature, and let $\Gamma$ be a discrete group. For every continuous map $f:X\to B\Gamma$, must $f_*[X]=0$ in $H_{\dim X}(B\Gamma;\mathbb Q)$? The classifying space $B\Gamma$ has fundamental group $\Gamma$ and contractible universal cover. The assertion concerns rational homology and includes both spin and nonspin manifolds.

title: Scalar Curvature Question [?13]: [∗] no closed aspherical15 manifold admits a metric withSc > 0

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Must every closed smooth aspherical manifold admit no Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature? Aspherical means that the universal cover is contractible.

title: Scalar Curvature Question [?34]: Bounds on Width and on the Macroscopic Dimension

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For every dimension $n$, consider complete Riemannian $n$-manifolds $X$ with scalar curvature bounded below by $\sigma>0$. Must the macroscopic dimension satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm{mc}}X\leq n-2$? Is there a dimension-dependent constant bounding the stated $(n-2)$-dimensional width by $C_n\sigma^{-1/2}$? The question also asks for the weaker $(n-1)$-dimensional width bound at this same scale. Width measures the size of fibers of a map to a lower-dimensional polyhedron.

title: Scalar Curvature Question [?35]: Bound on the Filling Radius forSc ≥σ > 0

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement:
Let $X$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold with scalar curvature bounded below by a positive constant. Does there exist a constant $C_n$, depending only on dimension, such that its filling radius satisfies
\[\operatorname{FillRad}(X)\leq C_n\bigl(\inf_{x\in X}\operatorname{Sc}(x)\bigr)^{-2}?\]
The filling radius measures the neighborhood size needed to fill the fundamental cycle after the metric-space embedding used in its definition.

title: Scalar Curvature Question [?91]: Prove that there is a dimension-dependent constant $c_n$ such that every compact Riemannian $n$-manifold $X$ w

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Prove that there is a dimension-dependent constant $c_n$ such that every compact Riemannian $n$-manifold $X$ with $\operatorname{Sc}(X)\geq-\sigma^2$ satisfies $\lVert X\rVert\leq c_n\sigma^n\operatorname{vol}(X)$, where $\lVert X\rVert$ is the simplicial volume.

title: Wikipedia geometry item 7: Fujita conjecture regarding the line bundle $K_{M} \otimes L^{\otimes m}$ constructed from a po…

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $M$ be a smooth projective complex variety of dimension $n$, $L$ an ample line bundle, and $K_M$ the canonical line bundle. Must $K_M\otimes L^{\otimes m}$ be globally generated for $m\geq n+1$ and very ample for $m\geq n+2$?

title: Wikipedia geometry item 13: Nagata's conjecture on curves, specifically the minimal degree required for a plane algebraic c…

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement:
For $r\geq10$ very general points $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ in the complex projective plane, is the degree $d$ of every plane curve with assigned multiplicities $m_i$ constrained by
\[d\sqrt r\geq\sum_{i=1}^rm_i?\]
In its usual nontrivial formulation the inequality is strict for effective curves in the range with nonzero multiplicities.

title: Wikipedia geometry item 14: Nagata–Biran conjecture that if $X$ is a smooth algebraic surface and $L$ is an ample line bund…

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Nagata–Biran conjecture that if $X$ is a smooth algebraic surface and $L$ is an ample line bundle on $X$ of degree $d$, then for sufficiently large $r$, the Seshadri constant satisfies $\varepsilon(p_1,\ldots,p_r;X,L) = d/\sqrt{r}$.

title: Zariski multiplicity conjecture on the topological equisingularity and equimultiplicity of varieties at singular points

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: If two complex hypersurface germs have the same embedded topological singularity type, must their multiplicities at the singular point agree? The multiplicity is the least degree of a nonzero term in a local defining equation. The related family version asks whether topological equisingularity forces equimultiplicity.

title: Finding matching upper and lower bounds for k-sets and halving lines

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For a finite planar point set, a $k$-set is a subset of $k$ points separable from the others by a line. Determine matching upper and lower bounds for the maximum number of $k$-sets, and for the number of halving lines that split the remaining points equally.

title: Automorphism Problem for the Turing Degrees

category.name: logic
category.description: Problems in mathematical logic, model theory, proof theory, and finite model theory.

statement: Determine the automorphism group of the partial order of Turing degrees.

title: Shelah's categoricity conjecture for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$

category.name: logic
category.description: Problems in mathematical logic, model theory, proof theory, and finite model theory.

statement: Shelah's categoricity conjecture for $L_{\omega_1,\omega}$: If a sentence is categorical above the Hanf number then it is categorical in all cardinals above the Hanf number.

title: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture

category.name: logic
category.description: Problems in mathematical logic, model theory, proof theory, and finite model theory.

statement: Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture: For every cardinal $\lambda$ there exists a cardinal $\mu(\lambda)$ such that if an AEC K with LS(K)${} \le \lambda$ is categorical in a cardinal above $\mu(\lambda)$ then it is categorical in all cardinals above $\mu(\lambda)$.

title: Soft Phases in Two-Dimensional O(N) Models

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Do spin correlations in the classical Heisenberg model, and other $O(N)$ models with $N>2$, decay exponentially at every nonzero temperature, or do these models have soft phases like the XY model? Prove or disprove that the low-temperature perturbative expansion is asymptotically correct, and determine whether there is a nonzero-temperature critical point and, if so, its critical indices.

title: Long-Range Order for the Quantum Heisenberg Model

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: (A) Prove long-range order for the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in dimension $D>2$ at temperature $T>0$. (B) Prove long-range order for spin $1/2$ in two dimensions in the ground state. (C) Find a robust proof for these continuous-symmetry cases that does not require exact translation invariance.

title: Extended States with Extensive Disorder

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Establish, in some energy range, the existence of extended eigenstates or continuous spectrum for linear operators with extensive disorder, such as a discrete Schrödinger operator with an i.i.d. random potential acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$. Also clarify the borderline case $d=2$.

title: Localization in Two Dimensions

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Prove that the spectrum of the Anderson model in dimension $\nu=2$ is dense pure point.

title: Bounded Excess Electrons

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For the $N$-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with nuclear charge $Z$, let $N_0(Z)$ be the least $N$ after which adding electrons no longer lowers the ground-state energy. Prove that $N_0(Z)-Z$ remains bounded as $Z\to\infty$.

title: Asymptotics of Atomic Ionization Energy

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For the $N$-electron Coulomb ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$, determine the asymptotics of the ionization energy $\delta E(Z)=E(Z-1,Z)-E(Z,Z)$ as $Z\to\infty$.

title: One-Dimensional Lieb-Thirring Constants

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For spatial dimension $\nu=1$ and $1/2<\gamma<3/2$, determine the optimal constants $L_{\gamma,1}$ in the Lieb-Thirring inequality as predicted by the Lieb-Thirring conjecture.

title: Mutually Unbiased Bases in Dimension Six

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Construct a set of at least four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six, or prove that there are no seven mutually unbiased bases in $\mathcal{H}_6$.

title: Finiteness of a Shafarevich–Tate group needed by the lifting method

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Prove finiteness of the Shafarevich–Tate group of the elliptic-curve lift required by the Huang–Raskind method, in the general cases where it is not known.

title: The density hypothesis for zeroes of the Riemann zeta function

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement:
Let $N(\sigma,T)$ count zeros $\rho=\beta+i\gamma$ of the Riemann zeta function with $\beta\geq\sigma$ and $0<\gamma\leq T$, counting multiplicity. For every $1/2\leq\sigma\leq1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, must
\[N(\sigma,T)\ll_{\sigma,\varepsilon}T^{2(1-\sigma)+\varepsilon}\]
hold as $T\to\infty$?

title: Generalized Riemann hypothesis for Selberg class

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Generalized Riemann hypothesis for Selberg class: do the nontrivial zeros of all functions in Selberg class lie on the critical line $1/2 + it$ with real $t$?

title: Zilber–Pink conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Zilber–Pink conjecture that if $X$ is a mixed Shimura variety or semiabelian variety defined over $\mathbb{C}$, and $V \subseteq X$ is a subvariety, then $V$ contains only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties.

title: No critical infinite cluster on transitive graphs

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For every infinite vertex-transitive graph $G$, prove that Bernoulli percolation has no infinite cluster at criticality, i.e. $\theta_G(p_c(G))=0$.

title: Absence of bigeodesics in first-passage percolation

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Prove that natural i.i.d. first-passage-percolation models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, including exponential edge lengths, almost surely contain no two-sided infinite geodesic.

title: 5.16 (Walsh) — Hyperbolic groups with Kleinian-type boundaries

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: If $G$ is a Gromov-hyperbolic group whose boundary is homeomorphic to the limit set of a convex-cocompact Kleinian group, is $G$ virtually a convex-cocompact Kleinian group?

title: Problem 2 — (Billiards in general polygons).

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For a planar polygonal billiard, does there always exist a regular periodic trajectory, meaning one that avoids all vertices? If so, does some such trajectory persist under small deformations of the polygon? Determine the asymptotic number of periodic trajectories of bounded length. Describe generic trajectories in generic polygons and decide whether the billiard flow is ergodic. For triangles, genericity is with respect to Lebesgue measure on the open angle simplex.

title: Major problems 5 — The chromatic splitting conjecture, which is considerably more complicated to state.

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every chromatic height $n$ and prime $p$, does the chromatic splitting conjecture hold for the $p$-local sphere? Write $L_n$ for localization at $E(n)$ and $L_{K(n)}$ for localization at Morava $K(n)$. The natural map $L_{n-1}S\to L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S$ is predicted to exhibit $L_{n-1}S$ as a wedge summand, with the complementary spectrum given by the prescribed wedge of lower chromatic localizations and suspensions. This asks for the full splitting prediction, including its prescribed complementary summands.

title: Morava K- and E-theory 1 — Show that pi_* L_K(n) S^0 is finitely generated over the p-adics in each degree.

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every prime $p$, positive chromatic height $n\ge1$, and integer degree $k$, must $\pi_kL_{K(n)}S^0$ be a finitely generated module over the $p$-adic integers? Here $L_{K(n)}$ is localization of the sphere spectrum at the height-$n$ Morava $K$-theory.

title: Morava K- and E-theory 5 — Find the shadow of the thick subcategory theorem in the K(n)-local category.

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Fix a prime $p$ and a positive chromatic height $n\ge1$. In the category of dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra at $p$, classify thick tensor ideals. A thick tensor ideal is closed under cofibers, retracts, and tensoring with any dualizable object. Does their inclusion order give the expected chromatic filtration analogous to the thick-subcategory theorem for finite spectra?

title: Rationally connected irrational varieties with property (*)

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement:
Is there a rationally connected irrational variety $X$ with property (*)?

Recall Property (*) from a previous question was defined as follows.
\[
D(X) = \langle \mathscr A_1, \ldots, \mathscr A_m \rangle
\]
has a semiorthogonal decomposition
with $\mathscr A_i \hookrightarrow D(Y_i)$ such that ${\rm dim} Y_i \leq {\rm dim}X-2.$

title: A transcendental-rank obstruction to surface hosts

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For a very general cubic fourfold $X$, is there a surface $S$ such that the Kuznetsov component $Ku(X) \subset D(X)$ has an embedding $Ku(X) \hookrightarrow D(S)$?

title: A cyclotomic resolution-Betti obstruction for the global canonical index

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Fix a dimension $n$. For projective $n$-dimensional varieties with log-canonical singularities and numerically trivial canonical divisor $K_X$, is the index of $K_X$ bounded by a constant depending only on $n$? The index is the least positive integer $m$ for which $mK_X$ is Cartier and linearly trivial in the stated canonical-index setting.

title: A new-Lefschetz defect reduction for rational Hodge pairings

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $A$ be a CM abelian variety over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction $A_0$ in characteristic $p$, and let $c$ be an absolute Hodge class on $A$. For a complementary-dimensional Lefschetz class $x$ on $A_0$, the specialization pairing $x\cdot\overline c$ lies in $\mathbb Q_\ell$ for every $\ell\neq p$. Must it be rational and independent of $\ell$? The question also asks for the corresponding property for arbitrary abelian varieties with good reduction.

title: A classwise CM implication and a one-product coniveau certificate

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: In a setting where the Hodge conjecture implies the Tate conjecture, must the generalized Hodge conjecture also imply the generalized Tate conjecture? In particular, does this implication hold for CM abelian varieties? The generalized assertions concern coniveau, not only individual cycle classes.

title: Hot spots: high-dimensional refutation, product rules, and heat-flow quantifiers

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Let $\Omega$ be a bounded planar simply connected domain, or a bounded convex domain in $\mathbb R^n$ for $n\geq3$. Must every first nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of its Laplacian attain its global maximum and minimum on the boundary rather than in the interior? This is the stated eigenfunction form of the hot-spots question.

title: Lipschitz extension from Hilbert spaces into L1

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Does the pair $(L^2,L^1)$ have the Lipschitz extension property? Explicitly, is there a constant $C<\infty$ such that every Lipschitz map from every subset of the Hilbert space $L^2$ into $L^1$ extends to the whole $L^2$ with Lipschitz constant at most $C$ times the original constant?

title: Finite-dimensional embeddings of doubling Hilbert subsets

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Suppose a metric space $X$ is doubling, meaning that every ball can be covered by a fixed finite number of balls of half its radius. If $X$ admits a bi-Lipschitz embedding into a Hilbert space, must it admit a bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\mathbb R^m$ for some finite $m$?

title: Higher-dimensional quantitative bi-Lipschitz parameterization and a scalar-curvature obstruction

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Find higher-dimensional analogues of the Bonk--Lang theorem on bi-Lipschitz parametrization by Euclidean space, with explicit quantitative control of the bi-Lipschitz constants from the geometric hypotheses. The question asks for a parametrization result, rather than only a continuous or locally topological chart.

title: Correlation cancellation for multiplicative functions

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

title: GPY lower bounds and distances between Gaussian primes

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Can the Goldston--Pintz--Y\i ld\i r\i m method produce an asymptotic count of primes with specified spacing, or at least a lower bound of the correct order? The latter asks for a positive proportion of the admissible tuples under consideration to contain at least two primes. A second question asks whether the method can be adapted to obtain small distances between Gaussian primes.

title: Steinitz prefix bounds for arbitrary norms

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement:
Steinitz conjecture

Given vectors $v_1,...,v_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ and a norm $X$ satisfying $\sum_{i=1}^n v_i=0$ and $||v_i||_X\le 1$ for all $i$. Define $S_n(X,d)=min_{\pi\in S^n}max_{k=1,...,n}|| \sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}||_X$ where $S^n$ is the set of all permutations of $[n]$. Let $S(X,d)=sup_n S_n(X,d)$. Then, $S(X,d) =O(\sqrt{d})$.

title: Cycle--clique Ramsey numbers and an endpoint-fan certificate

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement:
Let $r(C_m,K_n)$ be the least number of vertices that forces a red cycle of length $m$ or a blue clique of size $n$ in every red-blue edge-coloring of a complete graph. Is
\[r(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1\]
for all $m\geq n$?

title: A four-point Hamming barrier in Euclidean Ramsey theory

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: A finite subset $X$ of Euclidean space is Ramsey if, for every number of colors $r$, some dimension $N$ forces a monochromatic congruent copy of $X$ in every coloring of $\mathbb R^N$. Is every finite set lying on a sphere Ramsey?

title: Four concyclic points and bounded Euclidean Ramsey witnesses

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: For every four-point subset $X$ of a circle and every finite number of colors $r$, must there exist a dimension $N$ such that every coloring of $\mathbb R^N$ with $r$ colors contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $X$?

title: van der Waerden numbers and sparse forcing sets

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Let $W(n,m)$ be the least $N$ such that every red-blue coloring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has either a red $n$-term arithmetic progression or a blue $m$-term progression, and put $W(n)=W(n,n)$. Is $W(n)\leq2^{n^2}$? Also study $W^*(n)$, the least cardinality of a finite subset of $\mathbb N$ whose every two-coloring has a monochromatic $n$-term progression, including its comparison with $W(n)$.

title: Polynomial growth of diagonal van der Waerden numbers

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Let $W(k)$ be the diagonal two-color van der Waerden number: the least $N$ forcing a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression in every two-coloring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is $W(k)$ bounded by a polynomial in $k$?

title: Finite-field factorization and sparse-polynomial root testing

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For a degree-$n$ polynomial over $\mathbb F_q$, is factorization possible deterministically in time polynomial in $n$ and $\log q$? Determine the unconditional complexity of factoring $x^2-a$, and the optimal exponent in randomized factorization over $\mathbb F_2$. For a collection of polynomials of degree two or three, is deciding whether all split into linear factors faster through their product or through separate tests? Finally, can one decide whether $x^\alpha+ax^\beta+b$ has a root in $\mathbb F_q$ in time polynomial in $\log q$, where $0<\beta<\alpha\leq q-1$ and $a,b\in\mathbb F_q$?

title: Prime-factor advice in power-residue quotients

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For a given prime $p$, how much auxiliary data suffices to reduce the solution of higher-degree equations modulo $p$ to an efficient computation, in analogy with a single quadratic nonresidue for quadratic equations? Does a deterministic subexponential-time algorithm find a quadratic nonresidue modulo $p$ without an unproved hypothesis?

title: Three zeta-like products, degree-count inversion, and the factorization boundary

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement:
Can one compute the zeta function of $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)$,
\[\zeta_n(s)=\prod_{p\mid n}(1-p^{-s})^{-1},\]
without first factoring $n$? For a polynomial $f\in\mathbb F_q[x]$, consider the analogous product over its monic irreducible factors. From this zeta data, can one recover the factorization of $f$ in deterministic polynomial time?

title: Logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality and equality cases

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with support functions $h_K,h_L$, define
\[tK+_0(1-t)L=\bigcap_{u\in S^{n-1}}\{x:\langle x,u\rangle\leq h_K(u)^th_L(u)^{1-t}\}.\]
Must its volume be at least $|K|^t|L|^{1-t}$ for $0\leq t\leq1$? The stated equality question asks whether equality occurs only for $K=L$ or for parallelograms with parallel sides.

title: Log-Minkowski inequality for symmetric convex bodies

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
Log-Minkowski inequality

Show that if $K$ and $L$ symmetric convex bodies in ${\mathbb{R}}^n$, then
$$
\int\limits_{S^{n-1}} \log{\frac{h_K(u)}{h_L(u)}}\,d\bar{V}_L(u) \geq \frac1n \log{\frac{|K|}{|L|}},
$$
where $\bar{V}_L$ is the cone-volume probability measure of $L$.

title: $L_p$ Brunn–Minkowski inequality for symmetric convex bodies

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,L\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ containing the origin in their interiors, let $h_K,h_L$ be their support functions. For $p>0$ and $0\leq t\leq1$, define the $L_p$ Wulff combination by
\[tK+_p(1-t)L=\bigcap_{u\in S^{n-1}}\{x:\langle x,u\rangle\leq(th_K(u)^p+(1-t)h_L(u)^p)^{1/p}\}.\]
At $p=0$, replace the right-hand side by $h_K(u)^th_L(u)^{1-t}$. Must $|tK+_p(1-t)L|\geq|K|^t|L|^{1-t}$ hold for every $p\geq0$?

title: An ultrafilter-free local criterion for O2-ultrapower embeddability

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
Does every separable C*-algebra embed into an ultrapower of
$\mathcal O_2$ with respect to an ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$?

title: Positive consistency of Naimark's problem and a local hereditary reduction

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
Is the following relatively consistent with ZFC?

Every C*-algebra $A$ that has a unique irreducible representation up to the
unitary equivalence is isomorphic to the algebra of compact operators on some
Hilbert space.

title: Word problem for arbitrary Artin groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Is the word problem solvable for all Artin groups?

title: Algorithms for the word problem in Artin groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Is there an explicit algorithm to solve the word problem for all Artin groups?

title: Second homotopy of Artin classifying complexes

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: $K(\pi,1)$ conjecturette: is $\pi_2$ of Deligne complex/Salvetti complex/hyperplane complement always trivial? Find a proof using geometric/combinatorial techniques.

title: Parabolic subgroup intersections in Artin groups, including Euclidean type

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: In an Artin group, a standard parabolic subgroup is generated by a subset of the standard generators, and a parabolic subgroup is a conjugate of such a subgroup. Must an intersection of two parabolic subgroups again be parabolic? In particular, does this hold for Artin groups of Euclidean type?

title: Parabolic intersections under nonpositive curvature assumptions

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Are intersections of parabolic again parabolic when the Deligne complex has some notion of non-positive curvature? (i.e., systolic, injective, CUB, $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$)

title: Finitely presented infinite simple amenable groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Does there exist an infinite simple amenable group that is finitely presented? A finitely generated example alone is insufficient. The source also proposes the derived subgroup of the full group of the Penrose tiling as a possible construction to test for these properties.

title: The virtually-nilpotent/free-semigroup alternative

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: \textbf{Conjecture:}A finitely presented group is either virtually nilpotent, or contains a free subsemigroup of order $2$.

title: Existence of infinite finitely presented torsion groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Is there an infinite finitely presented torsion group, meaning a group in which every element has finite order? The stated Grigorchuk conjecture predicts that no such group exists.

title: Universal optimality beyond rapidly decaying completely monotone potentials

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Can we extend the definition of universal optimality to potentials with slow decay (or functions that are not completely monotonic)?

title: ALE singularities: Type-II existence and a bounded-scalar scale-energy certificate

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: In dimension $4$, can there be an ALE space as singularity for Ricci Flow?

title: Finite traceless-Ricci budget and Ricci-flat bubbles under bounded scalar curvature

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does $\max_M R(\cdot,t)$ blow up as $t\to T$ the singular time?

title: Endpoint Ricci-energy balance and Weyl-dominated blow-ups under bounded scalar curvature

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Let $(M^n,g_t)_{t\in[0,T)}$ be a Ricci flow with $T<\infty$. Assume $R <1$ on $M\times [0,T)$. Characterize $g_t$ as $t\to T$.

title: A hyperbolic geodesic and the robust infinite branch

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: If a Finsler metric on $S^2$ has one hyperbolic prime closed geodesic, must it have infinitely many geometrically distinct prime closed geodesics? Prime means that the geodesic is not an iterate; hyperbolic means that the linearized return map has no eigenvalue on the unit circle.

title: Closed geodesics in a finite-volume torus ansatz

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does every complete Riemannian manifold of finite volume have a nonconstant closed geodesic? Must it in fact have infinitely many geometrically distinct closed geodesics? The source additionally asks analogous questions for finite-volume Finsler metrics, distinguishing reversible metrics and the noncompact irreversible case.

title: No conjugate points: flat-growth rigidity and the three-dimensional residue

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: If a Riemannian manifold has no conjugate points, must its underlying smooth manifold admit some Riemannian metric with nonpositive sectional curvature? The new metric need not be the original one.

title: One-equation reductions for the rational Hamilton quaternions and Lipschitz order

category.name: logic
category.description: Problems in mathematical logic, model theory, proof theory, and finite model theory.

statement: Let $\mathbb H_{\mathbb Q}$ be the Hamilton quaternion algebra over $\mathbb Q$, and let $\mathcal O=\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z+j\mathbb Z+k\mathbb Z$ be its Lipschitz order. Decide the solvability of arbitrary noncommutative polynomial equations with either rational or quaternion coefficients, and with unknowns constrained either to $\mathbb H_{\mathbb Q}$ or to $\mathcal O$. Also ask for existential definitions of $\mathbb Z$ in $\mathcal O$ and of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb H_{\mathbb Q}$, and for the analogous decision questions in $M_n(\mathbb Z)$ and $M_n(\mathbb Q)$.

title: Finite-fiber normalization for elliptic Diophantine encodings

category.name: logic
category.description: Problems in mathematical logic, model theory, proof theory, and finite model theory.

statement: Can elliptic curves replace Pell equations in the proof of the undecidability of Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Z$, allowing fewer variables or a smaller degree? Can this approach represent every recursively enumerable set by a Diophantine equation having only finitely many witnesses for each parameter?

title: Characterization of cones admitting lifted LMI representations

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Characterize all full-dimensional pointed closed convex cones that are linear images of affine sections of positive semidefinite matrix cones, equivalently cones admitting a lifted linear-matrix-inequality representation. Is this class strictly larger than the class of hyperbolicity cones?

title: Polynomial-time lifted LMI representations of convex cones

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Characterize full-dimensional pointed closed convex cones that admit lifted linear-matrix-inequality representations with polynomial-time complexity. Is this efficiently representable class strictly larger than the class of hyperbolicity cones?

title: Long-time existence and behavior of the Calabi flow

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement:
What is the behavior of $g_{j \overline k}(t)$ solving the Calabi flow,
\[\frac \partial {\partial t} g_{j \overline k} = \partial_j \partial_{\overline k} R?\]
Can long time existence be established for toric surfaces?

title: Boundary integrability and the explicit confocal-caustic dictionary

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Let a smooth closed convex curve $\Gamma\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ bound a billiard table. If a neighborhood of the boundary is foliated by caustics, must $\Gamma$ be an ellipse? A caustic is a curve with the property that a billiard trajectory tangent to it remains tangent after every reflection. The question also asks whether these caustics must be analytic.

title: Non-self-adjoint spectral theory: completeness, reconstruction, and matrix-function bounds

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Resolve the listed completeness, reconstruction, stability, approximation, and numerical-range questions for non-self-adjoint operators.

title: The Dirac-Brown invariant-subspace problem: a defect-attainment reduction

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with faithful trace $\tau$, and let $T\in\Gamma$ have Brown measure $\mu_T=\delta_0$. Must there exist a projection $P\in\Gamma$, $0<P<1$, whose range is invariant under $T$, equivalently $(1-P)TP=0$?

title: An arithmetic and angular reduction for the 3-4-5 triangular billiard

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Is the billiard flow on the triangle with side lengths $3$, $4$, and $5$ ergodic?

title: Directional and interval-exchange reductions for polygonal billiards

category.name: miscellaneous
category.description: Problems whose source classification does not fit the main mathematical categories.

statement: For polygonal billiards, classify the ergodic invariant probability measures and the closed invariant subsets of the billiard flow. In a rational polygon, the invariant components associated with fixed directions are part of this classification problem.

title: Strongly Balanced Almost-Uniform Vector Permutations

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Does every finite set of $m$-dimensional vectors of Euclidean norm at most $1$, whose vector sum has norm at most $1$, admit a permutation whose every prefix sum has norm at most $\sqrt{2.7m}$ and whose block sums are uniformly bounded by an absolute constant?

title: Bounded Complements for $\varepsilon-Log-Canonical$ Varieties

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For every dimension bound $d$ and $\varepsilon\geq 0$, does there exist a finite set of complementary indices $N_d(\varepsilon)$ such that every $\varepsilon$-log-canonical variety $X$ of dimension at most $d$, with $-K_X$ nef and big over $Z$, has a general bounded complement $(X,D/n)$ that is $\varepsilon$-log-canonical?

title: Strong Nakayama Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Does every Artin algebra $A$ have finite finitistic dimension? For every nonzero finitely generated $A$-module $M$, must there be an integer $n\geq0$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_A^n(M,A)\neq0$?

title: Linear-Programming Sharpness and Universal Lattice Optimality

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does the linear-programming auxiliary-function method prove universal optimality for a finite spherical configuration exactly when the linear-programming bound for spherical codes is sharp for that configuration; and does its Euclidean analogue prove universal optimality for the hexagonal lattice, the $E_8$ root lattice, and the Leech lattice?

title: Arithmetic-Formula Lower Bounds for Permanent and Determinant

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Prove superpolynomial lower bounds for the arithmetic-formula size of an explicit polynomial, in particular the permanent or determinant.

title: Baum–Connes Conjecture for Locally Compact Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: For every locally compact group $H$, the Baum–Connes assembly map from the equivariant $K$-homology of $EH$ to $K_*(C_r^*(H))$ should be an isomorphism.

title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb Q$, the order of vanishing of $L(E,s)$ at $s=1$ equals $\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)$, the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite, and the leading coefficient satisfies the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula.

title: Baum–Connes Conjecture for Torsion-Free Groups

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For a torsion-free discrete group $G$, the Baum–Connes assembly map from $K$-homology $K_*(BG)$ to $K_*(C_r^*(G))$ should be an isomorphism.

title: Z-Stability of Infinite Tensor Powers

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For a $C^*$-algebra $A$ in the stated infinite-tensor-power setting, is the infinite tensor product $A^{\otimes\infty}$ isomorphic to its tensor product with the Jiang--Su algebra $\mathcal Z$? This tensorial absorption property is called $\mathcal Z$-stability.

title: Singularity Probability of Random Symmetric Sign Matrices

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Let $Q_n$ be an $n\times n$ random symmetric matrix whose upper-triangular entries are independent Bernoulli variables taking values $\pm1$. Determine or estimate the probability that $Q_n$ is singular.

title: Limit Theorems for Random Walks in Random Environments

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For random walks in random environments in dimension $d>1$, establish laws of large numbers and central limit theorems in full generality, both quenched and annealed.

title: Bloch–Beilinson Torsion Conjecture for Albanese Kernels

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For a smooth projective variety $V$ over a number field $k$, is the kernel of its Albanese map $\varphi_V$ torsion?

title: Nonvanishing or Uniruledness for Smooth Projective Varieties

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Does every smooth projective variety $X$ either have a nonzero pluricanonical section in $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(mK_X))$ for some $m>0$, or is it covered by rational curves?

title: Birkhoff Integrable-Billiards Conjecture

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: The only integrable planar inner billiards should be those inside ellipses.

title: Affine Fibrations as Affine-Space Bundles

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be an affine, faithfully flat $\mathbb{A}^n$-fibration whose closed fibers are geometrically integral. Must $f$ be an $\mathbb{A}^n$-bundle?

title: Higher-Dimensional Cancellation for Affine Domains

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed and let $A$ be a finitely generated $k$-domain of dimension $d>2$. If adjoining $m>0$ polynomial variables gives $A[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\cong k[x_1,\ldots,x_{m+d}]$, must $A$ already be a polynomial ring in $d$ variables over $k$?

title: Stable Coordinate Conjecture for Complex Polynomials

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: If a polynomial $P\in\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ becomes equivalent to $x_1$ after adjoining finitely many variables, must $P$ already be a coordinate?

title: Caccetta–Häggkvist Conjecture for Directed Triangles

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: If $G$ is a digraph with $n$ vertices and no directed cycle of length at most $3$, must some vertex of $G$ have outdegree less than $n/3$?

title: Single-Solution Bounds for Diophantine Equations

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Can Matiyasevich’s theorem for exponential Diophantine equations—an equation with at most one solution in the variables for each parameter, while some parameter has a solution exceeding every prescribed total effectively computable bound—be improved to genuine Diophantine equations without exponentiation, possibly allowing finitely many rather than at most one solution?

title: Artin’s Primitive-Root Density for Two

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Does the set of primes $p$ for which $2$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ have natural density $C=0.3739\ldots$ among the primes?

title: Primitive-Root Density Formulas for Rank-One Tori

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $K$ be a number field, let $T$ be a rank-one torus over $K$, and let $A\in T(K)$ be nontorsion. For each prime $p$, put $B_p=\langle T(K),\sqrt[p]{A},Z_p\rangle\subset T(\overline K)$, where $Z_p$ is a nontrivial $p$-torsion point, let $B_\infty$ be generated by all $B_p$, let $E$ be the finite abelian cokernel of $\operatorname{Gal}(K(B_\infty)/K)\to\operatorname{Aut}_{T(K)}(B_\infty)$, and put $A_p=\operatorname{Aut}_{T(K)}(B_p)$. Is the density of primes $\mathfrak q$ of $K$ for which the reduction of $A$ generates $T(\mathbb F_{\mathfrak q})$ equal to $C_{T,A}\prod_p(1-1/\#A_p)$, where $C_{T,A}=\sum_{\chi\in E^\vee}\prod_{p:\,\chi(A_p)\neq1}-1/(\#A_p-1)$?

title: Parity Conjectures for Elliptic Curves over Number Fields

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For an elliptic curve $E$ over a number field $K$, do the parity conjectures hold: assuming finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group, is $(-1)^{\operatorname{rank}E(K)}=w(E/K)$, and, for every prime $p$, is the corresponding $p$-Selmer-rank parity equal to $w(E/K)$? The stronger version asks for the rank-parity equality without assuming finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group.

title: Pálfy–Pudlák Finite-Lattice Representation Problem

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: For every nonempty finite lattice $\Lambda$, do there exist a finite group $G$ and $H\leq G$ such that $\Lambda$ is isomorphic to the inclusion-ordered lattice of all subgroups between $H$ and $G$?

title: RSW Theory for Anisotropic Square-Lattice Percolation

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: In critical anisotropic bond percolation on the square lattice, let horizontal and vertical edge probabilities $p_h,p_v$ satisfy $p_h+p_v=1$, and let $H(a,b)$ be the event of an open horizontal crossing of $[0,a]\times[0,b]$. Does an RSW theorem hold for general $p_h,p_v$, namely a uniform positive a priori bound for square crossings and a conditional extension bound for $H(kn,n)$ for every $k$? More generally, is there a class of shapes for which both properties hold?

title: Ramsey Sets and Finite Transitive Embeddings

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: A finite set $S$ in Euclidean space is Ramsey if, for each integer $r\ge2$, there exists a dimension $N$ such that every coloring $c:\mathbb R^N\to\{1,\ldots,r\}$ contains a monochromatic isometric copy of $S$ at its original scale. The dimension may depend on $S$ and $r$; no regularity is required of the coloring. Is $S$ Ramsey if and only if it embeds in a finite set whose isometry group acts transitively?

title: Exponential Distribution of Normalized Prime Gaps

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: If $p_n$ is the $n$th prime, then the normalized prime gaps $(p_{n+1}-p_n)/\log p_n$ should be asymptotically distributed like an exponential random variable with density $e^{-x}$ for $0\leq x<\infty$.

title: Convexity of Injectivity Loci Under MTW

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For a complete Riemannian manifold satisfying the Ma--Trudinger--Wang curvature condition for squared distance, must every tangent injectivity locus be convex? At $x$, this locus consists of tangent vectors for which the radial geodesic remains minimizing up to its endpoint before the cut locus; convexity is in the vector space $T_xM$.

title: Wolff Cone-Decomposition and Local-Smoothing Conjectures

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For functions $f_k$ whose Fourier supports lie in $\delta$-plates of the truncated light cone in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, does $\lVert\sum_k f_k\rVert_p\leq C_\varepsilon\delta^{-\alpha(p)-\varepsilon}(\sum_k\lVert f_k\rVert_p^p)^{1/p}$ hold for $p>2(d+1)/(d-1)$, where $\alpha(p)=d(1/2-1/p)-1/2$? Does the stronger mixed-norm version with $(\sum_k\lVert f_k\rVert_p^2)^{1/2}$ and exponent $\beta(p)=(d-1)/4-(d+1)/(2p)$ hold for $p>2+4/(d-1)$? Do the associated Sogge local-smoothing and cone-multiplier estimates hold in their conjectured ranges?

title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of Hyperkähler Manifolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $X$ be a hyperkähler manifold of complex dimension $2n$. Is its algebraic dimension necessarily in $\{0,n,2n\}$? If $a(X)=n$, does the algebraic reduction admit a holomorphic model $f:X\to B$, where $B$ is a normal projective variety of dimension $n$, and hence define a Lagrangian fibration? Does parabolic $\operatorname{NS}(X)$ imply $a(X)=n$?

title: Variational Principles for Dilute Spin Systems

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For dilute ferromagnets and sparse spin glasses, does the GREM-associated trial order parameter give the correct variational formula for the pressure? Does the numerator have a direct differential-equation formulation analogous to the Parisi equation? For the dilute ferromagnet, can one prove $\log Z_{N+M}\leq\log Z_N+\log Z_M$ directly? How should the pressure variational principle be formulated to exhibit appropriate trial order parameters, an entropy-minus-internal-energy interpretation, or a Legendre structure?

title: Local $p$-Adic Section Conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $k$ be a local $p$-adic field and $X/k$ a smooth projective curve of genus at least $2$. Is the natural map from $X(k)$ to conjugacy classes of continuous sections of $$\pi_1(X/k)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gal}(\overline k/k)$$ a bijection?

title: Alperin Weight Conjecture and Perfect Localities

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: In modular representation theory, understand and prove Alperin's Weight Conjecture, including the more general form suggested by Frobenius categories; also determine whether a perfect locality (centric linking system) associated with a Frobenius category exists and is unique.

title: The Lex-Plus-Powers Betti Number Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Let $S=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be a homogeneous regular sequence with $2\leq e_1\leq\cdots\leq e_r$, and let $P=(x_1^{e_1},\ldots,x_r^{e_r})$. For every homogeneous ideal $I\supseteq F$, does there exist a unique lex-plus-$P$ ideal $L$ with the same Hilbert function, with $b_{i,j}(S/L)\geq b_{i,j}(S/I)$ for all $i,j$?

title: Parity of 2-Primary Tate–Shafarevich Groups

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For every elliptic curve $E/K$ over a number field, the $\mathbb{F}_2$-dimension of $\operatorname{Sha}(E/K)[2]$ is even.

title: Section Conjecture for Hyperbolic Curves Without Boundary Points

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: If $k$ is a number field or a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and $X$ is a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve over $k$ whose boundary has no $k$-rational point, does $a\mapsto s_a$ biject $X(k)$ with conjugacy classes of sections of $\pi_1(X/k)$?

title: Section Conjecture for Hyperbolic Curves

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $X/k$ be a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve over a number field or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$. Does the map sending a rational point to its decomposition-group section biject $X(k)$ with conjugacy classes of continuous sections of $\pi_1(X/k)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\overline k/k)$?

title: Decidability of Rational Points over Number Fields

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Given a variety $X$ over a number field $k$, is there an algorithm that decides whether $X$ has a $k$-rational point?

title: Transience Implies Ballisticity for Uniformly Elliptic RWRE

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For a uniformly elliptic i.i.d. random walk in random environment in dimension $d\geq2$, does transience in a direction $\ell$ imply ballisticity in that direction?

title: Weak Zariski Decompositions of Pseudo-Effective Divisors

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $D$ be a pseudo-effective relative real Cartier divisor on a normal variety $X/Z$. Must there exist a projective birational map $f:W\to X$ and a numerical decomposition $f^*D\equiv_Z P+N$ with $P$ nef over $Z$ and $N$ effective? Such a decomposition is called a weak Zariski decomposition.

title: Unique Games Approximation-Threshold Conjecture

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Unique Games Conjecture: for every finite CSP and every $\varepsilon>0$, a polynomial-time algorithm achieves within $\varepsilon$ of the approximation threshold beyond which approximation is UGC-hard, and this threshold factor can be efficiently approximated.

title: Naimark's problem for $C^*$-algebras

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: If all irreducible representations of a $C^*$-algebra are unitarily equivalent, must that algebra be isomorphic to the compact operators on a Hilbert space?

title: The Toms–Winter regularity conjecture

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For a simple unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra $A$, are finite nuclear dimension, absorption of the Jiang--Su algebra $A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$, and strict comparison equivalent?

title: Naimark's Problem for Nonseparable $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: In the nonseparable case, does every $C^*$-algebra whose irreducible representations are all equivalent have to be an algebra of compact operators?

title: Birkhoff Conjecture for Integrable Convex Billiards

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Are ellipses the only strictly convex billiard tables whose billiard map is completely integrable, with the phase space foliated by invariant curves and trajectories tangent to a family of caustics?

title: Rigidity and Assembly Conjectures for Discrete Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: For a torsion-free group $G$ and integral domain $R$, are $0$ and $1$ the only idempotents of $RG$? Do the negative K-groups of $\mathbb{Z}G$, the reduced group $K_0(\mathbb{Z}G)$, and $\operatorname{Wh}(G)$ vanish? Are higher signatures homotopy invariant, closed aspherical manifolds topologically rigid, and groups of type FP of type FF? Is every finitely presented Poincaré-duality group of dimension at least five the fundamental group of an aspherical homology ANR-manifold? Is every hyperbolic group with boundary $S^n$ the fundamental group of a closed aspherical manifold?

title: Surface Subgroups of Word-Hyperbolic Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Does every word-hyperbolic group $G$ admit an injective homomorphism from the fundamental group of a closed surface of genus at least two?

title: Strict Cost–$\ell^2$-Betti Inequalities for Free Group Actions

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Does there exist an infinite group with a free probability-measure-preserving action $\Gamma\curvearrowright(X,\mu)$ such that $\beta_1^{(2)}(\Gamma)<\operatorname{cost}(R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright(X,\mu)})-1$?

title: Multipoint Seshadri Constants and Nagata-Type Conjectures

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For sufficiently many sufficiently general points $Z$ on a polarized variety $(X,L)$, is the Seshadri constant $\varepsilon(X,L;Z)$ maximal possible? In $\mathbb{P}^{2}$ this includes Nagata's conjecture for $r\geq10$ general points and the SHGH prediction for plane linear systems.

title: Brennan-Type Integrability for Crescent-Domain Conformal Maps

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Let $G$ be the bounded complementary component of a crescent domain and let $\phi:G\to\mathbb D$ be conformal. For which $\tau$ is $$\int_G|\phi'(z)|^{3+\tau}\,dA(z)<\infty$$ independently of $G$?

title: Forcing Graphs for Quasirandomness

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: For a finite graph $H$, let $t_H(G)$ be the number of graph homomorphisms $H\to G$ divided by $|V(G)|^{|V(H)|}$. Characterize those $H$ for which, for each fixed density $p$, the two conditions $t_{K_2}(G_n)\to p$ and $t_H(G_n)\to p^{|E(H)|}$ force every finite graph homomorphism density to tend to its value in a random graph of density $p$.

title: Forcing Conjecture for Bipartite Cyclic Graphs

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: A graph $H$ is forcing if its expected homomorphism density together with edge density forces quasirandomness of a graph sequence. Are the forcing graphs exactly the bipartite graphs containing a cycle?

title: Rational Ellipticity, Entropy, Euler Characteristic, and Formality

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Are almost nonnegatively curved manifolds rationally elliptic; do they admit Riemannian metrics with vanishing topological entropy; do nonnegatively curved manifolds have nonnegative Euler characteristic; and are positively curved manifolds formal?

title: Algebraic K-Theory and Rigidity Conjectures for Discrete Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.
