statement: For a torsion-free group $G$ and an integral domain $R$, are $0$ and $1$ the only idempotents of $RG$? Do the negative K-groups of $\mathbb{Z}G$, the reduced group $K_0(\mathbb{Z}G)$, and $\operatorname{Wh}(G)$ vanish? Are higher signatures homotopy invariant, closed aspherical manifolds topologically rigid, and groups of type FP of type FF? Is every finitely presented Poincaré-duality group of dimension at least five the fundamental group of an aspherical homology ANR-manifold? Is every hyperbolic group with boundary $S^n$ the fundamental group of a closed aspherical manifold? Are the Farrell–Jones assembly maps in algebraic K- and L-theory bijective?

title: Uniform Rectifiability from Bounded Riesz Transforms

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Let $n,d$ be integers with $1\le n<d$, and let $\mu$ be an $n$-dimensional AD-regular measure in $\mathbb R^d$. Is $\mu$ uniformly $n$-rectifiable if and only if its maximal $n$-Riesz transform $R_\mu^*$ is bounded on $L^2(\mu)$?

title: Higher-Dimensional Riesz Transforms and Uniform Rectifiability

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Let $0<n<d$ be integers with $n\neq d-1$, and let $E\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be $n$-Ahlfors regular. If its $n$-dimensional Riesz transforms are bounded on $L^2(E)$, must $E$ be uniformly $n$-rectifiable? Ahlfors regularity means that its $n$-dimensional measure in balls is comparable to the $n$th power of their radius; uniform rectifiability requires quantitative large pieces of Lipschitz images.

title: Hill Conjecture for Complete Graph Crossing Numbers

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Is the crossing number of every drawing of $K_n$ at least $\frac14\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-3)/2\rfloor$?

title: Classification of Class-VII Complex Surfaces

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Classify compact complex surfaces of class $\mathrm{VII}_0^+$: minimal compact complex surfaces with first Betti number one, negative Kodaira dimension, and positive second Betti number. Determine their geometric structure.

title: Inductive Proofs of Alperin Conjectures

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Prove the Alperin–McKay and Alperin weight conjectures, including their blockwise versions, by verifying the corresponding inductive conditions on finite simple groups.

title: Inductive Blockwise Alperin Weight Condition

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Does the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition hold for every finite simple group and every prime $p$, and hence imply the blockwise Alperin weight conjecture?

title: Uniqueness of Tangent Flows in Mean Curvature Flow

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Do mean-curvature-flow singularities have unique tangent flows, and more generally can the full asymptotic-symmetry conjecture for finite-time geometric PDE singularities be proved?

title: The Zariski Multiplicity Problem

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Do hypersurfaces with topologically equivalent isolated singularities necessarily have the same multiplicities at their singular points?

title: De Giorgi Conjecture for Allen–Cahn

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement:
If a bounded solution of
$$\Delta u+(1-u^2)u=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N$$
satisfies $\partial_{x_N}u>0$, must all level sets of $u$ be hyperplanes when $N\leq8$?

title: Log Abundance for Semi-Log-Canonical Pairs

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective semi-log-canonical pair with $\Delta$ a $\mathbb Q$-divisor. If $K_X+\Delta$ is nef, must $K_X+\Delta$ be semi-ample?

title: Euclidean Ramsey Configurations and Sphericity

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Which finite point configurations $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ are Ramsey for Euclidean $r$-colorings? In particular, are the Ramsey configurations exactly the spherical configurations?

title: Toms–Winter Regularity Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every unital, simple, separable, nuclear $C^*$-algebra $A$, are the following conditions equivalent: $A$ has finite nuclear dimension; $A\otimes\mathcal Z\cong A$; and $A$ has strict comparison?

title: $\mathcal Z$-Stability and Regularity of Nuclear $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Does $\mathcal Z$-stability imply finite nuclear dimension for all unital simple separable nuclear $C^*$-algebras? More broadly, does the equivalence between $\mathcal Z$-stability and strict comparison hold without the additional hypotheses currently known?

title: Kadison–Kastler Conjecture for Separable $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For a separable Hilbert space $H$, does there exist $\delta>0$ such that every pair of separable $C^*$-algebras $A,B\subset B(H)$ with $d(A,B)<\delta$ are spatially isomorphic?

title: The Kadison–Kastler conjecture for $C^*$-algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For a separable Hilbert space $H$, is there $\delta>0$ such that every pair of separable $C^*$-subalgebras $A,B\subseteq B(H)$ at Kadison--Kastler distance less than $\delta$ are spatially isomorphic? This distance is the Hausdorff distance between their closed unit balls in operator norm; spatial isomorphism means conjugacy by a unitary on $H$.

title: Trace-Cone Classification after Razak–Jacelon Stabilization

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For separable nuclear $C^*$-algebras $A$ and $B$, does $T(A)\cong T(B)$ if and only if $A\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K\cong B\otimes\mathcal W\otimes\mathcal K$, assuming the trace-cone isomorphism is a linear homeomorphism?

title: Jiang–Su Embeddings in Character-Free Central Sequence Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: If $F(A)$ has no characters, must it contain a unital copy of $\mathcal Z$? Does $\mathcal Z$ embed unitally into $\bigotimes_{n=1}^{\infty}D$ for every unital $C^*$-algebra $D$ without characters?

title: Subhomogeneous Character-Free Subalgebras of Infinite Tensor Powers

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Let $B$ be a separable unital $C^*$-algebra without characters and with separating tracial states. Does $B\otimes_{\min}B\otimes_{\min}\cdots$ contain a subhomogeneous $C^*$-algebra without characters?

title: Comparison Properties and Jiang–Su Absorption

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every nonelementary, stably finite, simple, separable, unital, nuclear $C^*$-algebra, are $\mathcal Z$-absorption, local weak comparison, and strict comparison equivalent? In particular, are local weak comparison and strict comparison equivalent?

title: Nuclear Dimension after Jiang–Su Stabilization

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Is $\operatorname{dim}_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A\otimes\mathcal Z)<\infty$ for every nuclear $C^*$-algebra $A$? What is the decomposition rank of $C(X)\subset C(X,M_n)$? Is it less than $\dim X$, or does dimension drop only after tensoring with a UHF algebra?

title: Variance Conjecture for Log-Concave Random Vectors

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Does there exist an absolute constant $C$ such that every centered log-concave random vector $X\in\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $\operatorname{Var}(|X|^2)\leq C\lambda_X^2\mathbb E|X|^2$, where $\lambda_X^2$ is the largest eigenvalue of its covariance matrix?

title: Dual-Graph Generation of Tautological Relations

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $\mathcal S_{g,n}$ be the strata algebra and let $\mathcal R\subset\mathcal S_{g,n}$ be the ideal generated by pullbacks and pushforwards of the dual-graph relations $R(g,n,r)$. Is $\mathcal R$ exactly the kernel of the natural surjection $\mathcal S_{g,n}\to R^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$? Do the analogous completeness statements hold after restriction to compact-type and rational-tail loci?

title: Minimum Graph Homomorphism Counts at Fixed Density

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: For a fixed finite graph $F$ and an $n$-vertex graph $G$ with at least $\rho n^2/2$ edges, determine the minimum possible number of graph homomorphisms $F\to G$, where homomorphisms need not be injective and need not preserve nonedges.

title: Displacement Exponents for Low-Dimensional Self-Avoiding Walks

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement:
For self-avoiding walk in dimensions $d=2$ and $d=3$, prove that there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that

$$n^{2/d+\varepsilon}\leq \mathbb E_n[\operatorname{Dist}(\gamma_n,0)^2]\leq n^{2-\varepsilon}$$

for all sufficiently large $n$.

title: Lefschetz Classes and the Tate and Hodge Conjectures

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For CM-type abelian varieties, the Lefschetz-class property that all Tate classes on all powers of a reduction, respectively all Hodge classes on all powers over the complex numbers, are generated by degree-one classes is a sufficient condition for the Tate, respectively Hodge, conjecture.

title: Rigidity of Completely Close $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For $C^*$-algebras $A,B\subseteq B(H)$, what structural properties and invariants are forced by small completely bounded Kadison–Kastler distance $d_{\mathrm{cb}}(A,B)$, and must sufficiently close algebras be isomorphic?

title: Regularity Properties of Nuclear $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For a separable unital simple nuclear stably finite infinite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra $A$, are the following equivalent: $\mathcal Z$-stability ($A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z$), strict comparison, and finite decomposition rank?

title: Homogeneity of Fano Contact Manifolds

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Must every smooth Fano contact manifold be homogeneous? Fano means that the anticanonical bundle is ample; a contact structure is a maximally nonintegrable holomorphic hyperplane distribution. Homogeneous means that a complex algebraic group acts transitively.

title: Sidorenko's Inequality for Bipartite Graphs

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement:
For every bipartite graph $H$ and graph $G$, does Sidorenko's inequality
$$t_H(G)\geq t_{K_2}(G)^{|E(H)|}$$
hold?

title: Linear Cycle-and-Edge Decompositions of Graphs

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Does every graph on $n$ vertices decompose into $O(n)$ cycles and edges? This is known for random graphs and for graphs with linear minimum degree.

title: Nonsingularity and Limit Laws for Random Matrices

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Let $A(n,d)$ be the adjacency matrix of a uniformly random $d$-regular graph, where $d>2$. Is $A(n,d)$ nonsingular with probability tending to $1$ as $n\to\infty$? What are the limiting distributions of the permanent of a random $\{\pm1\}$-matrix and the determinant of a random symmetric $\{\pm1\}$-matrix?

title: Almost-Everywhere Fourier Convergence in $L^{1}$

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Characterize the functions $f\in L^1(\mathbb T)$, for $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, whose Fourier series converges almost everywhere.

title: Fujita's Global Generation and Very-Ampleness Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $L$ be an ample line bundle on a complex manifold $X$. Is $K_X\otimes L^m$ globally generated for $m\geq\dim X+1$ and very ample for $m\geq\dim X+2$?

title: Enumeration of Graphs with Prescribed Degree Sequences

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Determine, exactly or asymptotically, the number of simple labelled graphs with a prescribed nonnegative degree sequence $\mathbf d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$.

title: Spectrahedrality of Hyperbolicity Cones

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Let $h$ be a real homogeneous polynomial hyperbolic in a direction $e$, meaning that $h(e)>0$ and $t\mapsto h(x-te)$ has only real zeros for every real vector $x$. Must its closed hyperbolicity cone be expressible as $\{x:\sum_i x_iA_i\succeq0\}$ for real symmetric matrices $A_i$? Such a cone is spectrahedral.

title: Vanishing of the $hat A$-Genus Under Nonnegative Curvature

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does the $\hat A$-genus vanish for every spin manifold that admits a metric of nonnegative sectional curvature?

title: Gromov Macroscopic Dimension Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: If a closed $n$-manifold $M$ admits a metric of positive scalar curvature, must the macroscopic dimension of its universal cover satisfy $\dim_{\mathrm{mc}}(\widetilde M)\leq n-2$?

title: Abundance Conjecture for Projective Minimal Models

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: If $X$ is a projective minimal model with nef canonical divisor $K_X$, is $K_X$ semiample; equivalently, is $mK_X$ globally generated for some $m>0$?

title: Rational Curves on Compact Kähler Manifolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $X$ be a compact Kähler manifold. Is $X$ covered by rational curves if and only if $K_X$ is not pseudoeffective? If $K_X$ is pseudoeffective but not nef, must $X$ contain a rational curve?

title: Solvability of Group Equations and Surjectivity of Word Maps

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Can every nonsingular equation $w\in\Gamma*F_n$ with coefficients in a group $\Gamma$ be solved over $\Gamma$? Also, for every nontrivial word $w\in F_2$, does there exist $n_0$ such that the word map $w:\operatorname{PU}(n)\times\operatorname{PU}(n)\to\operatorname{PU}(n)$ is surjective for every $n\geq n_0$?

title: The mod-$\ell$ Bogomolov–Pop conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from $\ell$. Does the natural map from field isomorphisms, modulo Frobenius in positive characteristic, to Milnor-$K$-theory-preserving isomorphisms $K^*/(K^*)^\ell\to L^*/(L^*)^\ell$ give a bijection?

title: The chromatic splitting conjecture

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement:
For the $p$-local sphere, let $L_nS$ be the chromatic localizations, let $L_{K(n)}S$ be Morava-$K(n)$ localization, and let $F_n$ be the common fiber in the chromatic fracture square. Does the natural map include $L_{n-1}S$ as a wedge summand of $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S$, so that
\[L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S\simeq L_{n-1}S\vee\Sigma F_n,\]
with the complementary spectrum admitting the predicted wedge decomposition into lower chromatic localizations?

title: Chromatic Splitting of the Local Sphere

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For the $p$-local sphere spectrum, let $L_nS$ denote its chromatic localizations and let $F_n$ be the common fiber in the chromatic fracture square. Does $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S\simeq L_{n-1}S\vee\Sigma F_n$, with $\Sigma F_n$ admitting the predicted wedge decomposition into lower chromatic layers?

title: Chromatic Fiber Structure at Bad Primes

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: At primes p that are bad relative to chromatic level n, give a plausible systematic description of the homotopy type of $\Sigma F_n$, where $F_n$ is the common fiber in the chromatic splitting square for the p-local sphere.

title: Bogomolov–Gieseker Inequality for Tilt-Semistable Threefold Complexes

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: BG inequality conjecture: let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb C$, let $B,\omega\in\operatorname{NS}(X)_{\mathbb Q}$ with $\omega$ ample, and let $E$ be tilt-semistable with $\nu_{\omega,B}(E)=0$. Then $\operatorname{ch}^{B}_{3}(E)\leq\frac{1}{18}\operatorname{ch}^{B}_{1}(E)\cdot\omega^{2}$. The conjecture is known for $X=\mathbb P^{3}$, smooth quadrics, and étale quotients of abelian threefolds.

title: Strong Locality and Reconstruction of Vertex Operator Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Is every unitary vertex operator algebra strongly local? Does every irreducible conformal net arise from a unitary vertex operator algebra through the conformal-net construction?

title: Eigenvalue Counts for Low-Degree Random Regular Graphs

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For uniformly random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, improve the estimates for the number of adjacency eigenvalues in a specified interval in the low-degree regime $d\lesssim(\log n)^4$. The target is a quantitative eigenvalue-counting estimate in that regime.

title: Injectivity of the Baum–Connes Assembly Map

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every discrete group $\Gamma$ and $i\in\{0,1\}$, is the Baum–Connes assembly map $\mu:K_i^\Gamma(E\Gamma)\to K_i(C_r^*(\Gamma))$ injective, where $E\Gamma$ is the universal space for proper $\Gamma$-actions?

title: Strong Cosmic Censorship at Weak Regularity

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For generic perturbations of Kerr initial data whose maximal globally hyperbolic developments have continuously extendible Cauchy horizons, are those developments nevertheless inextendible by Lorentzian metrics of regularity $C^0\cap W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}$? More generally, for generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data, is the maximal globally hyperbolic development inextendible as a weak solution of the Einstein vacuum equations?

title: Full-Measure Families of Ergodic Irrational Polygons

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Does there exist a set of full Lebesgue measure consisting of ergodic non-rational polygons with any prescribed number of edges?

title: Petty's projection-body conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq3$, let $\Pi K$ be its projection body. Is the affine-invariant ratio $|\Pi K|/|K|^{d-1}$ minimized exactly by ellipsoids? The support function of $\Pi K$ in a direction is the $(d-1)$-volume of the orthogonal projection of $K$ onto its perpendicular hyperplane.

title: Petty’s Projection-Body Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq3$, is the affine invariant $P(K)=|\Pi K|/|K|^{d-1}$ minimized exactly by ellipsoids?

title: Color Savings and Strong Chromatic Index Bounds

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: For a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and clique number $\omega$, how many colors can be saved in ordinary, list, or correspondence coloring relative to bounds from $\Delta$, $\omega$, and maximum average degree; in particular, is the strong chromatic index at most $1.25\Delta^2$?

title: Packing and Covering for Infinite Matroids

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Let $M$ and $N$ be matroids on a common ground set $E$. Does there exist a partition $E=P\mathbin{\dot\cup}C$ such that the restrictions $M|P$ and $N|P$ have disjoint spanning sets, while the contractions $M.C$ and $N.C$ have independent sets whose union is $C$?

title: Stanley–Stembridge Chromatic Symmetric Function Conjecture

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Stanley–Stembridge conjecture: if $G=G(m)$ is the incomparability graph associated with a Hessenberg function $m$, then its chromatic symmetric function $X_G(x)$ is a nonnegative sum of elementary symmetric functions.

title: Polynomial Algorithms for Mean-Payoff Games and Linear Programming

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm for solving mean-payoff games? Does there exist a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming?

title: Hemisphere Partition Functions and Stability Across GLSM Phases

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: In the GLSM setting, is the hemisphere partition function $Z_{D^2}:K_0(D)\to\mathbb C$ a central-charge function for a Bridgeland stability condition on $D$, and for the grade-restriction subcategory $W_n$ are the phase quotient categories $D_{\zeta\gg0}$ and $D_{\zeta\ll0}$ related to $W_n$ by the conjectured commuting equivalences?

title: Donovan’s Finiteness Conjecture for Fixed Defect Groups

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Fix a prime $p$, an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite $p$-group $P$. Among all finite groups $G$, are there only finitely many Morita-equivalence classes of blocks of $kG$ with defect group isomorphic to $P$?

title: Multistationarity and Permanence in MESSI Reaction Networks

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: For MESSI mass-action biochemical systems, characterize when a stoichiometric compatibility class can contain more than one positive steady state with the same conserved quantities, and determine the related permanence and invariant-subspace properties.

title: Absolute Continuity Parameters for Bernoulli Convolutions

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For $\lambda\in(0,1)$, let $\mu_\lambda$ be the distribution of $\sum_{n\geq0}A_n\lambda^n$, where the $A_n$ are independent unbiased random variables taking values $\pm1$. Determine the set of parameters $\lambda$ for which $\mu_\lambda$ is absolutely continuous.

title: Real Baum–Connes Isomorphism Conjecture

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: For every countable discrete group $G$, is the real Baum–Connes assembly map $\operatorname{KO}_*^G(\underline EG)\to \operatorname{KO}_*(C_r^*(G;\mathbb R))$ an isomorphism?

title: Finiteness of Atypical Hodge Subvarieties

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For an irreducible smooth quasi-projective variety $S$ with a variation $V$ of mixed rational Hodge structures, is the atypical locus $S_{\mathrm{atyp}}(V)$ a finite union of maximal atypical subvarieties, equivalently a proper algebraic subset and hence not Zariski dense; and, in the generalized André–Oort case, does Zariski density of CM points force $V$ to arise by pullback from a connected mixed Shimura variety?

title: Universal Bounds on Atomic Excess Charge

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Does there exist a universal constant $C$ such that a nucleus of charge $Z$ can bind at most $Z+C$ electrons in the full many-body Schrödinger theory?

title: Lech Multiplicity Conjecture for Flat Local Extensions

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Lech's conjecture: if $(R,\mathfrak m)\to(S,\mathfrak n)$ is a flat local extension of Noetherian local rings, then $e(R)\leq e(S)$.

title: Amenability of Thompson Group and Interval Homeomorphism Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Is Thompson's group $F$ amenable? Is the group $\mathrm{PL}_+(I)$ of orientation-preserving piecewise-linear homeomorphisms of the interval amenable?

title: Finiteness of Optimal Points in Shimura Subvarieties

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $S$ be a Shimura variety and $V\subseteq S$ a subvariety. Call a subvariety $W\subseteq V$ optimal in $V$ if every subvariety $Y$ with $W\subsetneq Y\subseteq V$ has larger defect $\delta(Y)=\dim\langle Y\rangle-\dim Y$, where $\langle Y\rangle$ is the smallest special subvariety containing $Y$. Does $V$ contain only finitely many points that are optimal in $V$?

title: Persistence and Permanence of Weakly Reversible Reaction Networks

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: For a weakly reversible mass-action reaction network, must every positive trajectory be persistent, staying away from the boundary in the long-time limit? Must it also be permanent, eventually remaining between uniform positive lower bounds and finite upper bounds within the relevant stoichiometric class? Weak reversibility means that every reaction edge belongs to a directed cycle.

title: $L^p$ Bounds for the Triangular Hilbert Transform

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Determine the range of exponents for which the triangular Hilbert transform, the trilinear singular integral with kernel $(x+y+z)^{-1}$, is bounded on the corresponding $L^p$ spaces.

title: Cartan–Hadamard Isoperimetric Conjecture

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement:
Does every Cartan–Hadamard manifold $(M^{n+1},g)$ satisfy
$$
|\Omega|\leq n^{-(n+1)/n}\omega_{n+1}^{-1/n}|\partial\Omega|^{(n+1)/n}
$$
for every bounded sufficiently regular open set $\Omega\subset M$?

title: Universal-Cover Decomposition for Nef Anticanonical Manifolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement:
If $X$ is a compact Kähler manifold with nef anticanonical class, does its universal cover decompose as

$$\widetilde X\simeq\mathbb C^q\times\prod_jY_j\times\prod_kS_k\times Z,$$

where each $Y_j$ is an irreducible Calabi–Yau manifold, each $S_k$ is an irreducible hyperkähler manifold, and $Z$ is rationally connected?

title: Kobayashi Pseudometric Vanishing on Calabi–Yau Manifolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Does the Kobayashi pseudometric vanish identically on every compact Calabi–Yau manifold? In particular, must every such manifold be Kobayashi non-hyperbolic and contain an entire curve?

title: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Automorphic L-Functions

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For every automorphic $L$-function having an Euler product, the Ramanujan bounds, analytic continuation, and a functional equation, do all nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line $\operatorname{Re}(s)=1/2$?

title: Nuclear Dimension of Transformation-Group Crossed Products

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For a continuous action of a locally compact group $G$ on a locally compact Hausdorff space $X$, when does the crossed product $C_0(X)\rtimes G$ have finite nuclear dimension?

title: Toms–Winter Regularity Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every nonelementary simple separable unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra $A$, are finite nuclear dimension, tensorial absorption of the Jiang–Su algebra $\mathcal Z$, and strict comparison of positive elements equivalent? When $A$ is stably finite, is finite decomposition rank equivalent to these conditions as well?

title: Uniform Property Gamma for Nuclear $C^*$-Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Does every simple separable unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra have uniform property $\Gamma$; that is, for every $k\geq2$, does its central sequence algebra contain $k$ pairwise orthogonal positive contractions whose trace is $1/k$ for every limit trace?

title: Absolute Continuity and Densities of Bernoulli Convolutions

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For $1/2<\lambda<1$, let $\nu_\lambda$ be the distribution of $\sum_{n\geq0}\varepsilon_n\lambda^n$, where the $\varepsilon_n$ are independent fair signs. Determine exactly when $\nu_\lambda$ is absolutely continuous, and classify the possible regularity of its density.

title: Minimum Distinct Distances Among Planar Point Sets

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Determine the minimum number $f(n)$ of distinct distances determined by $n$ distinct points in the Euclidean plane.

title: Falconer Distance Conjecture in the Plane

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: If $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ is a Borel set with Hausdorff dimension greater than $1$, must its distance set $$D(K)=\{|x-y|:x,y\in K\}$$ have positive Lebesgue measure?

title: Distances in Decorated Random Planar Maps

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Determine the order of typical graph distances in decorated random planar-map models, including $O(n)$ loop models and FK percolation on random planar maps.

title: Rank-One Equivalences for Elliptic Curves

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ and $r\in\{0,1\}$, the following are conjectured equivalent: $\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb{Q})=r$ and the Tate–Shafarevich group $\operatorname{Sha}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ is finite; $\operatorname{corank}_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\operatorname{Sel}_{p^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})=r$; and $\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(s,E/\mathbb{Q})=r$.

title: Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: The Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture asserts for every elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ that $\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb{Q})$, together with a formula for the leading Taylor coefficient in terms of arithmetic invariants; the rank part remains largely open when the rank is at least 2.

title: Equivalence of Affine-Space Embeddings Under Automorphisms

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Given embeddings $f,g:\mathbb C^d\hookrightarrow\mathbb C^n$, does there exist an automorphism $\Psi:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C^n$ such that $\Psi\circ f=g$?

title: Almost Everywhere Regularity of Parametrized Stationary Varifolds

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: For a general parametrized integer stationary $n$-varifold, does the singular set have zero $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure without additional hypotheses?

title: Mass–Angular-Momentum Inequalities with Trapped and Multiple Horizons

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For axisymmetric initial data with ADM mass $m$ and total angular momentum $J_\infty$, prove $m\geq\sqrt{|J_\infty|}$ for manifolds with a trapped inner boundary. For multiple black holes satisfying $m\geq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{many}}$, determine the value and parameter dependence of $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{many}}$ and identify the geometric meaning of its minimizer.

title: $d$-to-$1$ Games Conjecture

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For every integer $d\geq2$ and every $s>0$, does there exist an alphabet size $k$ such that it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable $d$-to-$1$ Label-Cover instances from instances of value at most $s$?

title: Mahler’s Volume Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement:
For every convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, is its Mahler volume bounded by

$$\bar s(K)=\lvert K\rvert\inf_{x\in K}\lvert(K-x)^\circ\rvert\geq\frac{(n+1)^{n+1}}{(n!)^2},$$

with equality for a simplex?

title: Planar Log-Brunn–Minkowski After Translation

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For planar convex bodies $K,L\in\mathcal K_2$, can the origin be positioned and $L$ translated so that $K$ and the translate satisfy the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality?

title: The $L_p$ Brunn–Minkowski Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement:
For $0\leq p<1$, origin-symmetric convex bodies $K,C\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, and every $\lambda\in[0,1]$, is

$$V\bigl((1-\lambda)K+_p\lambda C\bigr)\geq V(K)^{1-\lambda}V(C)^\lambda,$$

where $+_p$ denotes the $L_p$-linear combination?

title: Hadwiger’s Coloring Conjecture and Its Odd-Minor Variant

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: For every integer $t\geq1$, is every graph with no $K_{t+1}$ minor properly $t$-colorable? Is every graph with no odd $K_{t+1}$ minor properly $t$-colorable?

title: Optimal Fourier Restriction Estimates on Submanifolds

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement:
For the Fourier restriction operator $R$ to a submanifold $C\subset\mathbb R^{1+n}$, determine the optimal exponents $p,q$ for which

$$\lVert Rf\rVert_{L^p(C)}\lesssim\lVert f\rVert_{L^q(\mathbb R^{1+n})}$$

holds.

title: Birkhoff Rigidity Conjecture for Convex Billiards

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Are the completely integrable billiards inside smooth strictly convex planar domains exactly the billiards inside ellipses?

title: Local Birkhoff Rigidity Near Elliptical Billiards

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Let a smooth strictly convex planar billiard have invariant caustics with every rotation number in $(0,\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$. Under what hypotheses does this boundary foliation force the billiard table to be an ellipse?

title: Arnold Fixed Point Bound by Cup Length

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Does every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a closed connected symplectic manifold $M$ have at least $\operatorname{cl}(M)$ fixed points, where $\operatorname{cl}(M)$ denotes its cup length?

title: Chromatic Fixed-Point Implications for Finite p-Groups

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Let $H<G$ be subgroups of a finite $p$-group and let $m,n$ be nonnegative integers. For which pairs $(m,n)$ does $$K(m)_*(\Phi^H X)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad K(n)_*(\Phi^G X)=0$$ hold for every finite $G$-spectrum $X$?

title: Realizing Chromatic Types at Nested Fixed Points

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Let $H<G$ be subgroups of a finite $p$-group. For which pairs $(m,n)$ does there exist a finite $G$-spectrum $X$ such that $\Phi^H X$ has chromatic type $m$ and $\Phi^G X$ has chromatic type $n$?

title: Equivalence of Nuclear Dimension, Z-Stability, and Strict Comparison

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For simple, separable, nonelementary, nuclear $C^*$-algebras, are finite nuclear dimension, $\mathcal Z$-stability, and strict comparison equivalent?

title: Nagata Conjecture for Multipoint Seshadri Constants

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Nagata's conjecture asks whether, for $r\geq 10$ and sufficiently general points $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ in $\mathbb{P}^2$, the multipoint Seshadri constant of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ equals $1/\sqrt r$.

title: Fujita's Conjecture for Effective Global Generation

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For an ample line bundle $L$ on a projective variety $X$, what tensor power $L^{\otimes\ell}$ is guaranteed to be globally generated or very ample? In particular, does Fujita's conjecture hold for a smooth $n$-dimensional projective $X$, with $\omega_X\otimes L^{\otimes\ell}$ globally generated for $\ell\geq n+1$ and very ample for $\ell\geq n+2$?

title: Residual Finiteness and Minimal Presentations of Hyperbolic Groups

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Is every hyperbolic group residually finite? Separately, what is the smallest total relator length in a presentation of an infinite hyperbolic group with Kazhdan property (T)?

title: Maximum Excess Charge of Atoms

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For a Coulomb atom with nuclear charge $Z$, determine the largest number of electrons that can remain bound in a many-electron ground state. In particular, is the excess above $Z$ bounded by a universal constant independent of $Z$?

title: The Tamed-to-Compatible Symplectic Conjecture

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: If an almost-complex structure $J$ on a compact $4$-manifold is tamed by a symplectic form, does there exist a symplectic form compatible with $J$?

title: Artin Groups in Helly and Injective Geometry

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Which two-dimensional Artin groups of hyperbolic type are virtually Helly; which Artin groups act properly on CAT(0) cube complexes; are parabolic subgroups stable under intersection; is the complex of proper parabolic two-dimensional Artin subgroups NPC; is the three-generator all-label-3 Artin group Helly; are all two-dimensional Artin groups systolic; is reducibility equivalent to direct-product decomposition; are Artin groups and dihedral Artin groups hierarchically hyperbolic; do non-Helly groups act geometrically on coarse Helly graphs; are uniform lattices in $SL_n(K)$ injective or in $GL_n(K)$ Helly; and what are the injective hulls of $GL_n(R)/O(n)$ and the hyperbolic plane, and the Coxeter groups realizable as reflection groups in injective metric spaces?

title: Monge Minimizers for Multimarginal Coulomb Transport

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Do Monge-type minimizers always exist for the multimarginal optimal-transport problem with Coulomb cost?

title: Generic Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: For mean curvature flow, are the generic singularity models shrinking spheres and generalized shrinking cylinders? Determine whether other singularity types can be excluded by generic perturbation of the initial hypersurface.

title: Positive Scalar Curvature Obstruction for Aspherical Manifolds

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every closed smooth aspherical manifold $M$ of dimension $n\geq 4$, $M$ admits no Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

title: The Restricted Geometric Langlands Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $X/k$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, and let $G$ be reductive, with $\operatorname{char}(k)$ greater than the Coxeter number of $G$. In the corresponding derived $\ell$-adic setting, prove the canonical equivalence $\operatorname{Shv}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{Bun}_G)\simeq\operatorname{IndCoh}_{\operatorname{Nilp}}(\operatorname{LocSys}^{\operatorname{restr}}_{\widehat G})$.

title: Analytical Performance Theory for QAOA and RQAOA

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Develop an analytical account of the performance and limitations of QAOA and RQAOA in the resource-limited NISQ regime.

title: KLS Isoperimetric Coefficient Bound for Log-Concave Measures

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For a log-concave probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb R^d$, let its Cheeger coefficient be the infimum of $\mu^+(A)/\min(\mu(A),1-\mu(A))$ over measurable sets, where $\mu^+(A)$ is the outer boundary measure. Must this coefficient be at least an absolute positive constant times the same infimum restricted to half-spaces? The constant is required to be independent of the dimension and of $\mu$.

title: KLS Isoperimetric Coefficient Bound for Log-Concave Measures

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave probability measure on $\mathbb R^d$. Write $h(\mu)$ for the Cheeger infimum of boundary measure divided by the smaller mass of a set and its complement, and $h_{\mathrm{half}}(\mu)$ for that infimum restricted to half-spaces. Is there a universal $c>0$ for which $h(\mu)\geq c\,h_{\mathrm{half}}(\mu)$ for all $d$ and $\mu$?

title: Hadwiger’s Graph-Coloring Conjecture

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Does every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=t$ contain $K_t$ as a minor?

title: Kaplansky's Conjectures for Group Rings

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Let $G$ be a group and $K$ a field. If $G$ is torsion-free, must $K[G]$ have no nontrivial units, no nonzero zero divisors, and no idempotents other than $0$ and $1$; and for arbitrary $G$, must $K[G]$ be directly finite?

title: Spectral-Deformation Methods for the Riemann Hypothesis

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Can the spectral-deformation method based on $H_\lambda(t)$ prove the Riemann hypothesis despite the failure of the analogous assertion for $H_0(t)$ in general?

title: Zilber-Pink Unlikely Intersection Conjecture

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: For subvarieties of mixed Shimura varieties and semiabelian varieties, prove the Zilber--Pink finiteness prediction for maximal atypical intersections with special subvarieties. An intersection is atypical if its dimension exceeds the dimension expected from the ambient space. The general question encompasses the relevant Mordell--Lang and Andr\'e--Oort settings, rather than only a single family of ambient varieties.

title: Erdős–Gallai Cycle-Decomposition Conjecture

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Can every $n$-vertex graph be decomposed into $O(n)$ cycles and edges?

title: Boundedness of Multilinear Hilbert Transforms

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For $n\geq3$, establish the conjectured $L^p$ boundedness of the $n$-linear Hilbert transform; more generally, establish boundedness of the simplex Hilbert transform.

title: Fractal Schrödinger Convergence Above Half Dimension

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For $d/2<\alpha\leq d$, determine the sharp exponent $s(\alpha)$ such that every $f\in H^s(\mathbb R^d)$ satisfies $e^{it\Delta}f(x)\to f(x)$ as $t\to0$ for $\mathcal H^\alpha$-almost every $x$.

title: Uniform Bounds for Two-Dimensional Bilinear Hilbert Transforms

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Can one obtain uniform bounds for the forms associated with the entire family of two-dimensional bilinear Hilbert transforms?

title: Fourier Restriction Conjecture in Higher Dimensions

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For a smooth compact hypersurface with nonzero curvature in $\mathbb R^d$, prove the conjectured sharp $L^p$--$L^q$ Fourier restriction bounds in every dimension $d\geq3$. The restriction operator sends a Schwartz function to the restriction of its Fourier transform to the hypersurface; the requested range is the one dictated by the standard scaling and concentration obstructions.

title: Known Cases of Iitaka Subadditivity

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement:
For a surjective morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth projective varieties over a field of characteristic zero, with connected fibers and general fiber $F$, must the Kodaira dimensions satisfy
\[\kappa(X)\geq\kappa(Y)+\kappa(F)?\]
The Kodaira dimension measures the asymptotic growth of pluricanonical sections; the question is ordinary Iitaka subadditivity.

title: Singular Free Boundaries in the Critical Dimension

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Determine whether the critical dimension $d_*$ for singular free boundaries in the one-phase problem is $5$, $6$, or $7$; describe the singular set in the critical dimension; remove the symmetry assumption from the two-dimensional branch-point regularity result; and find a frequency-function proof that may extend to higher dimensions.

title: Zero–One Law for Directional Transience

category.name: probability
category.description: Problems involving probability theory, stochastic processes, and random structures.

statement: For a random walk in a random environment, let $A_+$ be the event of directional transience in a fixed direction. Must $\mathbb P(A_+)\in\{0,1\}$?

title: Fourier Restriction and Kakeya Incidence Conjectures

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Establish the Fourier restriction conjecture and Kakeya dimension conjecture in their full dimensional ranges. For restriction, determine the expected bounds for restricting Fourier transforms to curved hypersurfaces. For Kakeya, must a set in $\mathbb R^n$ containing a unit line segment in each direction have dimension $n$? The source poses these as an incidence-theoretic program, including the quantitative incidence bounds that underpin the two conjectures.

title: General Kakeya Dimension Conjecture

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^n$, and let $D$ be the set of directions in which $E$ contains a unit line segment. If $D\neq\varnothing$, must $\dim_{\mathrm H}E\geq\dim_{\mathrm H}D+1$?

title: Pointwise Convergence of Multiple Ergodic Averages

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: For commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ and bounded functions $f_1,\ldots,f_d$, do the averages $\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{k=1}^d f_k(T_k^n x)$ converge pointwise almost everywhere for every $d\geq2$?

title: Rigorous Mesoscopic Limits of Many-Particle Systems

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: Rigorously justify mesoscopic evolution equations, including the Boltzmann equation, as limits of many-particle systems.

title: Higher Finiteness Embeddings and TDLC Analogues

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Does every finitely presented group embed in a group of type $F_3$? Does every group of type $\mathrm{FP}_2$ embed in a group of type $\mathrm{FP}_3$? Formulate and prove, or disprove, a totally disconnected locally compact analogue of the intended embedding theorem.

title: Chromatic Number of Overlapping Unit-Circle Constellations

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Determine the maximum chromatic number of the tangency graph of a possibly overlapping constellation of unit circles. Equivalently, determine the chromatic number of the plane in the Hadwiger-Nelson problem.

title: Borsuk Partition Problem in Dimensions Four Through Sixty-Three

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: For each $4\leq d\leq 63$, determine whether every bounded set $S\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ can be partitioned into at most $d+1$ subsets of diameter strictly smaller than $\operatorname{diam}(S)$.

title: The Graphic Kahn–Kalai Conjecture

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Is there a universal $K>0$ such that, for every $H\subseteq K_n$, $p\geq Kp_E(H)\log v(H)$ implies $\Pr(G_{n,p}\supseteq H)\geq1/2$?

title: Finite-field polynomial multiplication and integer-multiplication lower bounds

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Can polynomials of degree less than $d$ over $\mathbb F_p$ be multiplied in $O(d\log p\log(d\log p))$ bit operations uniformly in $d$ and $p$, including $p=2$? The companion integer-multiplication question asks whether the cost $M(n)$ of multiplying $n$-bit integers must be $\Omega(n\log n)$. Both the uniform finite-field upper bound and the integer lower bound belong to this problem.

title: Rigidity of Stable One-Phase Solutions

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Let $u$ be a global stable solution of the one-phase free-boundary problem in $\mathbb R^n$. Prove that $u$ is one-dimensional when $n\leq 6$.

title: The Generalized Étale-Homotopy Section Conjecture

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Determine the classes of varieties $X/k$ for which the canonical map $X(k)\to\Gamma^{\mathrm{et}}(X/k)$ is a bijection, where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{et}}(X/k)$ is the set of homotopy classes of sections of the étale-homotopy fibration $\Pi^{\mathrm{et}}(X)\to\Pi^{\mathrm{et}}(k)$.

title: Existence of the Smith–Toda Complex $V(4)$

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Does the Smith–Toda complex $V(4)$ exist at any prime?

title: Arthur-Langlands Reciprocity

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Establish the general Arthur-Langlands reciprocity correspondence between constituents of the discrete automorphic spectrum of a connected reductive group $G$ and the appropriate global Galois or Arthur parameters, compatibly with localization and automorphic $L$-functions.

title: Low-Temperature Order in Quantum Heisenberg Ferromagnets

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For the short-range quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet in dimension $d\geq 3$, prove that sufficiently low temperature produces long-range order; specifically, prove that $\lim_{\Lambda\nearrow\mathbb{Z}^d}|\Lambda|^{-2}\sum_{x,y\in\Lambda}\langle\widetilde S_x\cdot\widetilde S_y\rangle_{T,\Lambda}>0$ for all sufficiently small $T>0$.

title: AQFT Locality of Unitary Vertex Operator Algebras

category.name: physics
category.description: Problems at the intersection of mathematics and physics.

statement: For every unitary vertex operator algebra, do the smeared vertex operators satisfy the strong locality needed to produce a conformal net of local von Neumann algebras? Strong locality requires the algebras associated with disjoint intervals to commute.

title: Structural Problems for $C^*$- and von Neumann Algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Do the normalized random matrices $X_k$ converge strongly to a free circular distribution? Are $q$-Gaussian $C^*$-algebras selfless for $-1<q<1$ and $q\neq0$? Are the indicated tracial ultrapowers mutually isomorphic? Does there exist a group that has a mixed identity and whose reduced $C^*$-algebra is selfless? Does $C^*(F_2\times F_2)$ have the local lifting property? Does a nonamenable group without free subgroups exist whose reduced $C^*$-algebra has rapid decay? For compact convex $K$, does equality of its minimal and maximal operator-system structures imply that $K$ is a Choquet simplex? Are the free group factors $L(F_2)$ and $L(F_3)$ nonisomorphic? Are the free-product factors $Z(r,\tau)^{*n}$ and $Z(r,\tau)^{*m}$ isomorphic, and is there a dichotomy? Is every unital simple separable $C^*$-algebra singly generated? Do classifiable $C^*$-algebras admit filtrations with rapid decay? Is $F_2$ superrigid among hyperbolic groups at the level of reduced $C^*$-algebras? When is a von Neumann algebra with a faithful state selfless?

title: Maximum Normalized Mahler Measure of Littlewood Polynomials

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Let $P_n(x)=\sum_{k=0}^n a_kx^k$ range over Littlewood polynomials with $a_k\in\{-1,1\}$. Determine the extremal limit superior $b_m=\limsup_{n\to\infty}M_0(P_n)/\sqrt{n}$, where $M_0$ denotes Mahler measure.

title: Pointwise Convergence of Polynomial Ergodic Averages

category.name: dynamical_systems
category.description: Problems about long-term behavior of deterministic systems, Hamiltonian dynamics, and periodic orbits.

statement: Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a probability space with commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\ldots,T_m$, and let $P_1,\ldots,P_m\in\mathbb{Z}[y]$. For $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in L^\infty(X)$, do the averages $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^m f_i(T_i^{P_i(n)}x)$ converge pointwise almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$?

title: Rank Distribution in Quadratic-Twist Families

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Fix an elliptic curve $E$ over a global field $K$, a norm $\operatorname{Nm}$ on $K$, and $j\geq0$. If $\mathcal{F}(X)$ is the set of quadratic extensions $K(\sqrt{d})/K$ with squarefree $d$ and $\operatorname{Nm}(d)\leq X$, determine the limit as $X\to\infty$ of the proportion for which $\operatorname{rk}E(K(\sqrt{d}))-\operatorname{rk}E(K)=j$.

title: Torsion-Anomalous Conjecture for Semiabelian Varieties

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let $V$ be an irreducible subvariety of a semiabelian variety $G$. Prove that $V$ contains only finitely many maximal $V$-torsion-anomalous subvarieties.

title: Optimal Covering Density of Euclidean Balls

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Determine the optimal asymptotic covering density of Euclidean space by congruent balls.

title: Bounded-Diameter Monochromatic Covers

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: For every integer $r\geq2$, does there exist $D(r)$ such that every $r$-edge-colored complete graph can be covered by $r-1$ monochromatic connected subgraphs, each of diameter at most $D(r)$?

title: Higher-dimensional Kakeya conjecture

category.name: analysis
category.description: Limits, continuity, calculus, and function theory.

statement: For every dimension $n\geq4$, must every subset of $\mathbb R^n$ containing a unit segment in each direction have full dimension $n$ in the Kakeya conjecture? The question covers all higher dimensions, not only one fixed dimension.

title: Median Actions and Residual Finiteness for Hyperbolic Groups with Sphere Boundary

category.name: group_theory
category.description: Problems about groups, group actions, representations, and related algebraic structures.

statement: Let $G$ be a hyperbolic group with boundary homeomorphic to $S^2$. Can one prove that $G$ admits an action with unbounded orbits on a median space, equivalently that $G$ does not have Kazhdan's property $(T)$? More generally, is every medianized hyperbolic group cubulable, or can one at least prove that it is residually finite?

title: Pure-power Hilbert functions for complex Artinian complete intersections

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: If $I\subset C[x_{1},\dots ,x_{n}]$ is homogeneous and contains a regular sequence of degrees $2\leq a_{1}\leq \cdots \leq a_{n}$, does some homogeneous ideal J containing $x_{1}^{a_{1}},\dots ,x_{n}^{a_{n}}$ have the same quotient Hilbert function as I?

title: Lex-plus-powers Betti bounds for Artinian quotients over C

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Let $S=C[x_{1},\dots ,x_{n}]$, $n\geq 1$, and let I contain a homogeneous regular sequence of degrees $2\leq a_{1}\leq \cdots \leq a_{n}$. Is there a $lex-plus-(x_{1}^{a_{1}},\dots ,x_{n}^{a_{n}})$ ideal L with the same Hilbert function as I and $\beta ^S_{i,j}(S/I)\leq \beta ^S_{i,j}(S/L)$ for every i,j?

title: Projectivity from simultaneous self-Ext and algebra-Ext vanishing

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every finite-dimensional algebra A over a field and every finite-dimensional left A-module M, does $Ext_A^i(M,M\oplus A)=0$ for all integers $i>0$ imply that M is projective?

title: A dimension-free quadratic bound for the canonical Foulkes–Howe map

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For all integers $a\geq 2$ and $b\geq a(a-1)$, and all finite-dimensional complex V, is the canonical multiplication-and-averaging map $Sym^{b}(Sym^{a}V)\to Sym^{a}(Sym^{b}V)$ surjective?

title: Complex group-ring traces vanish on infinite-order classes

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every discrete group G, every $q\geq 1$ and every idempotent $e\in M_q(C[G])$, is the sum of the diagonal coefficients of e over each infinite-order conjugacy class zero?

title: Deciding finite-algebra congruence-lattice representability

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Does an algorithm exist that, on every order table of a finite nonempty lattice L, halts and determines whether L is isomorphic to Con(A) for some finite algebra A with arbitrary finitary operations?

title: Higher Verlinde fiber functors in positive characteristic

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every prime p, every algebraically closed field k of characteristic p and every finite symmetric tensor category C over k, do there exist $n\geq 1$ and an exact faithful k-linear symmetric tensor functor $C\to Ver_{p^n}(k)$?

title: Foulkes inclusion for the sixth symmetric power

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every finite-dimensional complex vector space V and every integer $b\geq 6$, does there exist a GL(V)-equivariant injection $Sym^{6}(Sym^{b}V)\to Sym^{b}(Sym^{6}V)$?

title: Integral block finiteness over a fixed complete valuation ring

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Fix a prime p, a complete characteristic-zero discrete valuation ring O with algebraically closed residue field of characteristic p, and $M\geq 1$. Are there only finitely many O-linear Morita classes of finite-group block orders OGb whose residue defect groups have order at most M?

title: Integral K3 injectivity for regular local domains

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every Noetherian regular local domain A with fraction field F, is the canonical map $K_{3}(A)\to K_{3}(F)$ injective on integral algebraic K-theory, including ramified mixed characteristic?

title: Integral K5 injectivity for regular local domains

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every Noetherian regular local domain A with fraction field F, is the canonical map on integral algebraic K-groups $K_{5}(A)\to K_{5}(F)$ injective, including ramified mixed characteristic?

title: Finite central dimension of algebraic finitely generated division rings

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: If a division ring D is generated as an algebra by finitely many elements over its center F and every element of D is algebraic over F, must [D:F] be finite?

title: Finite torsion-class support for traces over l1 group algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every discrete group G and idempotent $e\in M_q(\ell ^{1}(G))$, $q\geq 1$, is there a finite set F of finite-order conjugacy classes such that the diagonal coefficient sum of e over every conjugacy class outside F is zero?

title: Finiteness of the little finitistic dimension

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every Artin algebra $A$, are the finite projective dimensions $\operatorname{pd}_A(M)$ of its finitely generated modules $M$ bounded above?

title: Every irreducible occurs in the staircase tensor square

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every $m\geq 1$, put $N=m(m+1)/2$ and $\rho =(m,m-1,\dots ,1)$. Does the tensor square of the complex Specht representation $S^\rho $ contain every irreducible representation of $S_N$; equivalently, is $g(\rho ,\rho ,\lambda )>0$ for every partition $\lambda $ of N?

title: Saturation factor one for even Spin groups

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement:
For $G=Spin(2n)$ over C, $n\geq 2$, and dominant integral weights $\lambda ,\mu ,
u $ whose sum belongs to the root lattice, does the existence of a G-invariant in $V(N\lambda )\otimes V(N\mu )\otimes V(N
u )$ for some integer $N\geq 1$ imply the existence of one in $V(\lambda )\otimes V(\mu )\otimes V(
u )$?

title: An irreducible tensor square containing every symmetric-group representation

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For each positive integer n outside\{2,4,9\}, does $S_{n}$ have an irreducible complex representation V such that $V\otimes V$ contains every irreducible complex representation of $S_{n}$?

title: Self-Ext vanishing over symmetric algebras

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: For every finite-dimensional symmetric algebra A over a field, must each finite-dimensional module M with $Ext_A^i(M,M)=0$ for every integer $i>0$ be projective?

title: Algebraicity of the prescribed Kuga–Satake map

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let S be any smooth projective complex K3 surface, with rational transcendental cohomology T(S). Choose standard Kuga–Satake Clifford, polarization and realization data, giving an abelian variety A and its prescribed rational Hodge map $\kappa :T(S)\to H^{2}(A×A,Q)$. Is $\kappa $ induced on T(S) by a rational codimension-two cycle on S×A×A? The assertion includes an isogenous realization with the map transported by its chosen rational Hodge isomorphism.

title: Algebraicity of split Weil-type eightfold classes

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For every imaginary quadratic field K and complex abelian eightfold A of split Weil type, with K acting with multiplicities (4,4) and a compatible split Hermitian polarization, is the Weil-class subspace $\wedge ^{8}_K$ $H^{1}(A,Q)\subset H^{8}(A,Q)$ contained in the image of $CH^{4}(A)\otimes Q$? All compatible polarization types and members with extra endomorphisms are included.

title: All ordinary Kähler klt fourfold programs terminate

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For a normal globally Weil-Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold with effective rational klt boundary and rational Cartier canonical adjoint, does every maximal ordinary negative-ray program terminate on the original input, retaining klt and global Weil Q-factoriality, with projective contractions of relative Bott–Chern dimension one? A pseudo-effective input must end nef; otherwise the endpoint must have a projective lower-dimensional Mori fiber contraction. Global strong Q-factoriality, if imposed, must persist.

title: All rational-boundary projective lc fourfold programs terminate

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For a projective lc fourfold with effective rational boundary over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, without assumed Q-factoriality or pseudo-effectivity, do all permitted negative extremal-ray programs have the required contractions and flips and finitely many birational steps, regardless of choices? Must every maximal program end with nef adjoint or a lower-dimensional relative-Picard-one Mori fiber contraction?

title: Rank-preserving contraction for anticanonical fibrations

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let X be smooth connected projective complex with no nonzero holomorphic q-forms for $q>0$ and smoothly semipositive $L=-K_X$; let an algebraic torus T act naturally on L. Take a T-invariant dominant rational $f:X\dashrightarrow Z$ to smooth connected projective Z with C(Z) relatively algebraically closed in C(X). On a resolution $Y\to X$ and $Y\to Z$, require a nonzero invariant positive L-multiple on the generic fiber and require invariant section dimension of $K_{Y/X}+mL$ on that fiber to be one for every positive multiple of some a. Must either X have a positive T-invariant anticanonical section, or f factor through a smooth projective W of smaller dimension retaining both generic-fiber properties and relative algebraic closure?

title: Integral Bloch statement for surfaces of geometric genus zero

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For every smooth connected projective complex surface S with $p_g(S)=0$, is the integral Albanese homomorphism $CH_{0}(S)^0\to Alb(S)(C)$ an isomorphism? In particular, if also $q(S)=0$, must degree give $CH_{0}(S)\cong Z$?

title: Arithmetic Stein-degree bounds for log Calabi–Yau boundaries

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For each $d\geq 1$ and real $t>0$, is there a finite integer N(d,t) bounding $dim_k$ $H^{0}(S^\nu ,O_{S^\nu })$ whenever (X,B) is a normal integral projective lc rational pair over a characteristic-zero field k with dim $X=d$, $H^{0}(X,O_X)=k$ and $K_X+B$ Q-linearly trivial, and S is a prime boundary component of coefficient at least t? This must also bound the Stein degree of $S\to Spec$ k.

title: Bounded local klt complements for Fano contractions

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: For every $d>0$ and positive rational $\varepsilon $, does an integer $N(d,\varepsilon )>0$ work for each normal integral $\varepsilon -lc$ Q-Gorenstein d-fold over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field with a projective connected-fiber contraction $f:X\to Z$ and relatively ample $-K_X$, so that near each closed base point there is effective rational B with (X,B) klt and $N(K_X+B)$ integral Cartier and linearly trivial?

title: Bounded-metric anticanonical nonvanishing for klt pairs

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Let (W,D) be projective Q-factorial klt with effective rational boundary and nef rational Cartier $P=-(K_W+D)$. If on a smooth projective resolution $\rho $ the pullback $\rho *P$ has a semipositive singular metric with locally bounded weights and $\chi (O_{Wtilde})\neq 0$, must some positive Cartier multiple mP have a nonzero global section?

title: Bounded denominators in low-dimensional log Calabi–Yau fibrations

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Fix \(1\le d\le4\) and a finite rational coefficient set \(\Phi\subset[0,1]\). Do positive integers \(p_0\mid p\) and a rational DCC set \(\mathcal B\subset[0,1]\), depending only on \(d,\Phi\), give every complex projective log canonical \(d\)-fold \((X,B_X)\) with coefficients in \(\Phi\), and every contraction \(f:X\to Z\) to a positive-dimensional normal projective base with \(K_X+B_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}f^*D\) for a rational Cartier divisor \(D\), an exact presentation \(K_X+B_X+p_0^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\psi)=f^*(K_Z+B_Z+M_Z)\)? The base divisor must be rationally linearly equivalent to \(D\), \(B_Z\) must be effective with coefficients in \(\mathcal B\), the resulting generalized pair must be log canonical and klt for klt input, and the moduli b-divisor must be b-nef with its \(p\)-multiple b-Cartier.

title: Campana–Peternell for Fano sixfolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Must every smooth connected projective complex Fano variety of dimension exactly six whose tangent bundle is nef be rational homogeneous?

title: Abelianity of special compact Kähler fundamental groups

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Must the fundamental group of every connected smooth special compact Kähler manifold have an abelian subgroup of finite index? Special has Campana's standard meaning, excluding fibrations with general-type orbifold base.

title: Canonical minimal models in numerical dimension one

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: If a smooth connected projective complex n-fold, $n\geq 3$, has pseudo-effective $K_X$ with Nakayama numerical Kodaira dimension $\kappa _\sigma (K_X)=1$, must a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips reach a projective Q-factorial terminal model Y with nef $K_Y$? On a common resolution must $p*K_X=q*K_Y+E$ hold with E effective q-exceptional and containing every contracted X-prime in its support?

title: Canonical nonvanishing for smooth fourfolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: If X is a smooth connected projective complex fourfold and $K_X$ is pseudo-effective, must $H^{0}(X,mK_X)$ be nonzero for at least one positive integer m?

title: The cohomological Hikita isomorphism for quivers

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement:
For any finite oriented quiver, allowing loops and multiple arrows, put $G=\prod GL(V_i)$ and $N=\oplus _{i	o j}Hom(V_i,V_j)\oplus _i$ $Hom(V_i,W_i)$. Let F be any linear flavor torus commuting with G, and choose a character $
u $ for which stable equals semistable in the zero cotangent moment fiber and G acts freely. Set $X=\mu ^-1(0)^{
u -stable}/G$. For the commutative flavor-deformed BFN Coulomb algebra $A_F$ without loop rotation, let $A_F^
u $ denote the quotient by its nonzero $
u$-weights, without reduction. Must the natural coefficient maps from $R=H*_{G×F}(point;C)$ onto $H*_F(X;C)$ and $A_F^
u $ be surjective with identical kernels, giving a graded R-algebra isomorphism? Empty X with zero ring is included.

title: Conditional good models for strongly Q-factorial Kähler fourfolds

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Assume full orbifold Iitaka subadditivity in Fujiki class C, the stated pseudo-effective klt fourfold MMP conditional on it, and abundance for nef klt fourfold adjoints after nonvanishing. For a normal connected globally strongly Q-factorial compact Kähler fourfold X with effective rational klt boundary B and Q-Cartier analytically pseudo-effective $K_X+B$, must there be a bimeromorphic good minimal model extracting no divisor, improving discrepancies strictly on contracted primes and having a globally generated positive Cartier adjoint multiple?

title: Kähler log abundance assuming logarithmic Iitaka

category.name: algebraic_geometry
category.description: Geometric objects defined by polynomial equations.

statement: Assume that for every connected-fiber surjective morphism $f:U\to V$ of smooth connected projective complex varieties with reduced effective SNC $D_U,D_V$ and $Supp(f*D_V)\subset Supp(D_U)$, the very general fiber F with $D_F=D_U|F$ satisfies $\kappa (U,K_U+D_U)\geq \kappa (V,K_V+D_V)+\kappa (F,K_F+D_F)$, taking $-\infty $ as absorbing. For every normal irreducible compact Kähler space X with an effective rational lc boundary $\Delta $ and Q-Cartier analytically nef $K_X+\Delta $, must some positive Cartier multiple of the actual adjoint line be globally generated?
