title: Polynomial deterministic two-way simulation of one-way NFAs

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Can every n-state one-way nondeterministic finite automaton be simulated by a deterministic two-way finite automaton with only polynomially many states, with the polynomial independent of the input alphabet?

title: Two-fifths-power space simulation for one writable tape

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For deterministic machines with one writable tape and head, finitely many read-only input heads moving by unit steps from fixed origins, cap-independent symbol functions and the prescribed local-access condition, can the finite-control and halting outcome by binary time cap T be simulated in $\widetilde O(T^{2/5})$ workspace bits, excluding read-only input storage, with unrestricted simulation time and no requirement to materialize the final tape?

title: Deterministic quasipolynomial mean-payoff games

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Do finite turn-based ordinary mean-payoff games with binary integer rewards admit deterministic quasipolynomial-time exact zero-threshold winning-set computation in the total binary input length?

title: Perfect-completeness two-to-one hardness

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For every fixed rational $\delta \in (0,1)$, is it NP-hard to distinguish value 1 from value $\leq \delta $ in an explicitly unweighted two-to-one projection game with fixed alphabets [2q] and [q], where every right answer has exactly two preimages?

title: Entropy bounds at perfect-matching marginals

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Let G be a loopless multigraph on 2m vertices and x in its perfect-matching polytope. Is the maximum entropy H(x) of a distribution of perfect matchings having edge marginals x between $F(x)-(2-2/m)B(x)$ and F(x), where $F(x)=-\sum _e$ $x_e$ $\log (x_e)$ and B is the sum of $-(1-x_e)\log (1-x_e)$? Natural logarithms are used and 0 log 0 is zero.

title: Cubic border-determinantal lower bound for the permanent

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Does the border-determinantal complexity of the m×m complex permanent grow at least c $m^{3}$ for one absolute $c>0$ and all sufficiently large m? Border complexity permits coefficient limits of affine-linear determinant representations.

title: Worst-case Subset Sum below the half exponent

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement:
Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be positive integers, let $t\ge0$, and assume $n\ge2$. The Subset Sum decision asks whether $\sum_{i\in I}a_i=t$ for some $I\subseteq[n]$. Put
\[
 b=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(1+\max(t,a_1,\ldots,a_n))\rceil\},\qquad
 w=\lceil4(n+b+\log_2(n+2))\rceil.
\]
Use a classical word RAM with $w$-bit words, read-only random-access input, charged word reads and writes, addressing, comparisons, arithmetic, bit operations and shifts. A fresh uniform random word costs one operation, and retained random words occupy writable memory. Seek a single uniform randomized program that halts on every execution, answers correctly with probability at least $2/3$ on every input, and satisfies
\[
 \forall c\in\mathbb N_{\ge1}\ \exists C_c>0,N_c\ \forall n\ge N_c,\ b\le n^c:\quad
 T\le C_c2^{0.49n}
\]
on every random path. All preprocessing is charged, and the program receives no value of $c$.

title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Must every Boolean threshold of a real multilinear degree-at-most-d polynomial on the uniform n-cube, with $sign(0)=1$ and $1\leq d\leq n$, have total influence at most $8d\surd n$?

title: Matrix hitting points in every positive characteristic

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Given a promised prime p in binary and n,s in unary, can one construct in polynomial bit time an n-tuple of d×d matrices over $F_p$, $d=O(n^{3}s^{6})$, on which every nonzero free noncommutative polynomial formula of size $\leq s$ over every field of characteristic p evaluates nonzero?

title: Quasilinear robust PCP for PPAD

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement:
An End-of-Line input $I$ consists of explicit Boolean circuits $P,S:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$, with $n\ge1$, $P(0)=0$, $S(0)\ne0$, and $P(S(0))=0$. Its length $N$ counts both full circuit encodings. A solution is nonzero $v$ with $P(S(v))\ne v$ or $S(P(v))\ne v$.

A generalized circuit has finitely many nodes and a nonempty equally weighted gate list, each node the output of at most one gate. Node values lie in $[0,1]$. The gate types are constants, scaling, copying, saturated sum and difference, comparison, and Boolean OR, AND and NOT; rational gate parameters lie in $[0,1]$. Arithmetic gates have additive tolerance $\varepsilon$. Comparison sends an input gap larger than $\varepsilon$ to the corresponding output interval $[0,\varepsilon]$ or $[1-\varepsilon,1]$. Boolean gates use low inputs $\le\varepsilon$ and high inputs $\ge1-\varepsilon$, with the usual Boolean implications; absent a required implication, any output in $[0,1]$ is allowed.

Seek fixed rational $0<\varepsilon<1/10$, $0<\delta<1$, integers $A>0,b\ge0$, a polynomial $p$, and deterministic construction and decoding algorithms $R,D$. If $M$ denotes the complete output encoding length, define an acceptable witness to be a rational node assignment of binary length at most $p(M)$ satisfying at least $(1-\delta)$ of the gates. The locations of violated gates are arbitrary and every node keeps one globally consistent value. Require existence of an acceptable witness for every circuit in this model and
\[
 |R(I)|\le AN\lceil\log_2(N+2)\rceil^b,\qquad
 D(I,x)\text{ solves }I\quad\text{for every acceptable }x\text{ of }R(I).
\]
Construction time is polynomial in $N$; decoding time is polynomial in $N$ and the supplied witness length. The constants and algorithms are uniform, without advice or randomized construction. The encoding bound is part of acceptability, not a claim about all real assignments.

title: Almost-linear maximum-cardinality matching

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Can one uniform randomized logarithmic-word RAM algorithm find an explicit maximum-cardinality matching in every finite general graph with probability $\geq 2/3$, halting on every path within $(n+m)^{1+o(1)}$ instructions?

title: Randomized k-server with squared-logarithmic ratio

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For every metric space with at least k+1 points, $k\geq 2$ and initial labeled server tuple, does there exist one randomized online policy whose expected cost on every oblivious finite request sequence is $\leq C(\log (k+1))^{2}OPT+B$, with a metric-independent absolute C and a finite B independent of sequence and horizon? Can B be zero when initial positions are distinct?

title: One rational matrix hitting point for noncommutative formulas

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For each $n,s\geq 1$, can one deterministically construct in polynomial bit time a single n-tuple of rational matrices of dimension at most $2ns^{2}$ that makes every nonzero size-s noncommutative polynomial formula over every characteristic-zero field nonzero, with polynomially bounded entry bit lengths?

title: Quadratic sensitivity versus block sensitivity

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Is there an absolute C such that every nonconstant total Boolean function satisfies $bs(f)\leq C$ $s(f)^{2}$, where s is sensitivity and bs block sensitivity?

title: Factor-two shortest common superstring

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Can a deterministic algorithm polynomial in the total encoded length of any finite collection of ordinary strings return a common superstring of length at most twice the minimum?

title: Quasipolynomial stochastic mean-payoff decision

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For explicitly encoded finite turn-based zero-sum stochastic mean-payoff games with binary rational rewards and transition probabilities, can the states of value at least zero be computed deterministically in quasipolynomial bit time in the total encoding length? The statement concerns threshold decision, without asserting polynomial time or exact value output.

title: Low-space worst-case Subset Sum at half-exponential time

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For positive-integer Subset Sum with n items and bit length $b\leq n^c$ for any fixed c, can one uniform randomized classical word algorithm use $n^{O_c(1)}2^{n/2}$ operations and $O_c((n+b+2)^{15}2^{0.199n})$ writable words on every path, never falsely answering YES and answering YES instances correctly with probability $\geq 2/3$, without being given c?

title: Independent-set hardness with a three-colorability promise

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For every fixed $\delta \in (0,1/3)$, can 3SAT be reduced in deterministic polynomial time to a nonempty finite simple unweighted graph so that satisfiable formulas yield three-colorable graphs and unsatisfiable formulas yield graphs with independence number $<\delta $ times the vertex count?

title: Polynomial-time three-machine unit-job scheduling

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For any explicitly listed finite acyclic precedence graph on unit-length nonpreemptive jobs, can one deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm produce a minimum-makespan schedule on three identical machines and decide every binary deadline exactly?

title: Polynomial state complementation of two-way NFAs

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Is there a polynomial p independent of the finite alphabet such that every n-state two-way nondeterministic finite automaton has an equivalent complement-recognizing two-way NFA with at most p(n) states?

title: Uniform finite-metric randomized k-server implementation

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For every finite rational metric and $2\leq k<n$, is there one randomized online bit algorithm with polynomial preprocessing in input length L and polynomial work per request in L+log(t+1), guaranteeing expected cost $\leq C(\log (k+1))^{2}OPT+B$ for every finite oblivious sequence, without knowing its horizon?

title: Uniform quasipolynomial worst-case trace reconstruction

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement:
For binary strings of known length $n\ge2$ and known rational retention probability $p\in(0,1]$, seek one randomized multitape Turing machine that reconstructs every input with probability at least $2/3$. At each fixed $p$, its independent ordinary deletion-trace budget should be
\[
 M(n,p)=\exp\bigl(O_p((\log n)^3(1+\log\log(2n))^6)\bigr).
\]
Its bit time must be polynomial in $n$, the binary encoding length of $p$, and the prescribed trace budget, on every internal random-bit sequence and every trace stream consisting of words of length at most $n$. Preprocessing, finite-precision computation, received bits and output are charged. Only external generation of independent traces is an oracle operation.

title: Constant-factor hardness of uniform sparsest cut

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For each fixed $C>1$, is approximating uniform sparsest cut within factor C NP-hard on explicitly encoded finite undirected graphs with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demand between each pair of distinct vertices?

title: Large Goemans–Linial gaps for uniform sparsest cut

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Do unit-demand capacity instances on unbounded vertex counts n have Goemans–Linial semidefinite integrality gap at least $c\surd \log (n)/(\log $ $\log (n))^{3}$ for one absolute $c>0$, with positive relaxation value?

title: EXPTIME-completeness of variable-dimensional WL

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Is k-WL equivalence with k supplied as part of the input EXPTIME-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, both for general finite uncolored graphs and when both graphs have maximum degree three?

title: Factor-two hardness of Vertex Cover

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For each fixed $0<\varepsilon\le1$, is it NP-hard, under deterministic polynomial-time reductions, to return a vertex cover of a finite simple unweighted graph whose size is at most $(2-\varepsilon)$ times the minimum? A vertex cover meets every edge. The graph is explicitly encoded; no degree bound or indistinguishability promise is imposed.

title: Zero dimension exponent for well-conditioned sampling queries

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement:
For $V\in C^{2}(R^d)$ with $V(0)=0$, $
abla V(0)=0$ and $I\leq 
abla ^{2}V(x)\leq 2I$ everywhere, can its Gibbs law be sampled to total-variation error $\leq 1/10$ using at most $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon $ exact $(V,
abla V)$ oracle queries on every execution, for each fixed $\varepsilon >0$, with unrestricted real computation between queries? Is the optimal query budget also at least c log d?

title: Complexity of Weisfeiler–Leman graph identification

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Is deciding whether a finite nonempty simple uncolored graph has WL identifying dimension at most a binary integer k EXPTIME-complete under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions, using ordinary color refinement in dimension one and joint tuple refinement at higher dimensions?

title: Parity witnesses for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For fixed $k\geq 4$, let $t=k+1$ under joint WL refinement or $t=k$ under separate refinement. Given finite domains $D_i$ and pairwise label maps $\lambda ^i_ij:D_i\to L_ij$, can one explicitly produce two equal-order uncolored simple graphs that are k-WL-equivalent exactly when no choice $d_i\in D_i$ satisfies $\lambda ^i_ij(d_i)=\lambda ^j_ij(d_j)$ for all $i<j$, with common graph order at most $A[t\cdot 2^{t-2+3binom(t-1,2)}+12binom(t,3)]$ when all domain and label cardinalities are $\leq A$?

title: Superpolynomial worst-case trace sample lower bounds

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: For each fixed deletion probability $q\in(0,1)$ and each fixed positive reconstruction success probability, is worst-case reconstruction of binary strings of length $n$ from deletion traces required to use at least $n^{c\log\log n}$ samples, for some $c>0$ and every sufficiently large $n$?

title: Elementary expansion for Grothendieck infinity-groupoids

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every Grothendieck coherator C, every cellular C-infinity-groupoid X and every n-cell $a:D_n\to X$, is $X\to X\cup _{D_n}D_{n+1}$, attached along the source inclusion of the next globe, a weak equivalence?

title: Curtis stable mod-two Hurewicz image

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Is the image of positive-degree stable sphere homotopy in $H*(Q_{0}S^{0};F_{2})$ generated only by the Hurewicz images of the Hopf-invariant-one elements $\eta ,\nu ,\sigma $ and the Kervaire-invariant-one elements that exist?

title: Filtered chromatic splitting at generic primes

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every $n\geq1$ and prime $p>n+1$, does $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ have an ordered cofiber filtration of $2^n$ stages indexed by $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, starting with cofiber $L_{n-1}S$ and the canonical localization unit as its first-stage map, with later cofibers $\Sigma^{-\sum_{i\in I}(2i-1)}L_{n-\max I}S$, and a single compatible family $y_i$ of degrees $1-2i$ whose products give the corresponding $K(t)$-local sphere bases for all $1\leq t<n$, using the derived $p$-complete sphere for every local sphere?

title: Hahn–Wilson thick generation at fp-type two

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For each prime p, must every connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two lie in the thick subcategory generated by $BP\langle 2\rangle _p^\wedge $? The claimed counterexamples occur at every sufficiently large prime and also have $L_{2}^fX\simeq L_{2}X$ and $L_{T(2)}X\simeq L_{K(2)}X$.

title: Finite assembly of the height-three chromatic overlap

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: At $p=3$, can $L_{2}L_{K(3)}S_{3}^\wedge $ be built from $L_{0}S_{3}^\wedge $, $L_{1}S_{3}^\wedge $ and $L_{2}S_{3}^\wedge $ by finitely many shifts, sums, cofibers and retracts in the category of E(2)-local modules over the derived three-complete sphere?

title: Rational injectivity of maximal coarse assembly

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every uniformly discrete bounded-geometry metric space X, is maximal coarse assembly $KX_{1}(X)\otimes Q\to K_{1}(C*max(X))\otimes Q$ injective? In particular this asks about coarse disjoint unions of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree.

title: Pure cosmetic surgery for knots in the three-sphere

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: If K is a nontrivial smooth knot in $S^{3}$ and Dehn fillings along slopes r and s are orientation-preservingly homeomorphic, must $r=s$?

title: Rational injectivity of reduced coarse assembly

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every uniformly discrete bounded-geometry metric space X, is reduced coarse assembly $KX_{1}(X)\otimes Q\to K_{1}(C*(X))\otimes Q$ injective, including coarse disjoint unions of finite connected bounded-degree graphs?

title: Singer vanishing in dimension four

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Does every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré-duality CW complex of formal dimension four have all L$^{2}$-Betti numbers zero outside degree two? This includes every closed aspherical topological four-manifold.

title: Thomason structures in all strict categorical dimensions

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: For every positive finite n and for strict infinity-categories, does the Thomason adjunction $c_n$ $Sd^{2}$ $\dashv $ $Ex^{2}$ $N_n$ supply a proper combinatorial model structure on strict n-categories with weak equivalences detected by the nerve, and a Quillen equivalence with the Kan–Quillen model category of simplicial sets?

title: Kervaire detection at the prime three

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Which members $b_j$ of the standard prime-three Kervaire-detection family survive to stable sphere homotopy, and which have additive-order-three representatives? The proposed answer is precisely $j=0,2,3$, in stems 10,106,322.

title: Wall D(2) problem with a finite target model

category.name: topology
category.description: Properties preserved under continuous deformations.

statement: Let $X$ be a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex and $\widetilde X$ its universal cover. If $H_i(\widetilde X;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $i>2$, and $H^3(X;M)=0$ for every $\mathbb Z[\pi_1X]$-module $M$, must $X$ be homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex of dimension at most two?

title: Navier–Stokes Existence and Smoothness

category.name: pde
category.description: PDEs and their applications in physics and geometry.

statement: Prove global smooth existence for every admissible unforced three-dimensional initial velocity, either in all of space or on the periodic torus; alternatively, produce admissible smooth initial data and forcing with no smooth global solution in either setting. Whole-space solutions must have bounded energy, and all source hypotheses and four accepted alternatives are included.

title: Continuum Hypothesis

category.name: set_theory
category.description: Foundations of mathematics, infinite sets, and cardinality.

statement: The continuum hypothesis says that every uncountable subset of the real numbers has the same cardinality as the real numbers. Its truth cannot be decided from ZFC alone, assuming ZFC is consistent.

title: Are there infinitely many perfect powers in the Fibonacci sequence?

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Determine whether 8 and 144 are the only Fibonacci numbers that are powers with both base and exponent greater than one. The complete classification is already known; the exceptional values 0 and 1 appear only under the broader convention allowing those bases.

title: The Moving Sofa Problem

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Find the greatest area of a single rigid planar shape that can be carried continuously around a right angle in a hallway of width one, and identify a shape attaining it.

title: The Köthe Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Must a ring with no nonzero nil two-sided ideal also have no nonzero nil one-sided ideal? The question concerns arbitrary associative rings, including rings without an identity.

title: Singular Cardinals Hypothesis

category.name: set_theory
category.description: Foundations of mathematics, infinite sets, and cardinality.

statement: Does the power set of every singular strong limit cardinal have the smallest cardinality it could have, namely the next larger cardinal? Its behavior is sensitive to additional set-theoretic assumptions.

title: Whitehead Problem

category.name: set_theory
category.description: Foundations of mathematics, infinite sets, and cardinality.

statement: If every abelian-group extension of a group by the integers splits, must that group have a basis over the integers? The unrestricted question is known to be independent of ZFC.

title: The Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture

category.name: computer_science
category.description: Computational complexity, algorithms, and theoretical CS.

statement: Can every pair of vertices of any bounded polytope be joined by an edge path whose length is bounded by one fixed polynomial in its dimension and number of facets?

title: The Jacobian Conjecture

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Does every polynomial map of complex affine space whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant have a polynomial inverse? The assertion quantifies over all positive dimensions.

title: The Cycle Double Cover Conjecture

category.name: graph_theory
category.description: Problems involving graphs, networks, and their properties.

statement: Can every graph with no bridge have its edges covered by a list of cycles so that each edge appears exactly twice?

title: Smale's 12th Problem: Centralizers of Diffeomorphisms

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Do diffeomorphisms whose only commuting diffeomorphisms are their own iterates form a dense set, a residual set, or a set containing an open dense subset, in each differentiability class?

title: Hilbert's 7th Problem: Transcendence of Certain Numbers

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Must raising an algebraic irrational number to an algebraic irrational power always give a transcendental number, for every complex value of the power? This historical question is answered affirmatively by the Gelfond--Schneider theorem.

title: Hilbert's 14th Problem: Finite Generation of Rings

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Is the ring of invariant polynomials for every linear algebraic-group representation generated by finitely many polynomials? The historical universal claim is false.

title: Hilbert's 17th Problem: Expression of Definite Forms

category.name: algebra
category.description: Group theory, ring theory, field theory, and algebraic structures.

statement: Can every real rational function that is nonnegative wherever defined be written as a finite sum of squares of real rational functions? Artin's solution of Hilbert's seventeenth problem gives an affirmative answer.

title: Large Sum-Free Sets

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Must every set of $n$ positive integers contain a sum-free subset whose size exceeds $n/3$ by an amount tending to infinity with $n$? Bedert's 2025 theorem gives an affirmative answer.

title: Restricted Sumset Problem

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Can every sufficiently large finite set of integers provide a subset of size at least the hundredth power of its logarithmic size such that no sum of two distinct chosen elements belongs to the original set?

title: Roth's Theorem with Random Common Differences

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Which independent random sets of allowed positive common differences preserve Roth's theorem for every positive-density set? The optimistic target permits inclusion probabilities only a diverging factor above $1/n$.

title: Lipschitz AP-Free Graphs

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Can an integer-valued function with a fixed bound on its slope have a graph containing no three equally spaced collinear graph points? Equivalently, can an increasing integer sequence with bounded gaps avoid every progression in which both the indices and the values form three-term arithmetic progressions?

title: Multidimensional Szemerédi Theorem Bounds

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Obtain density thresholds controlled by a fixed finite number of logarithms for multidimensional arithmetic configurations, including squares and three-dimensional corners over finite fields, and fixed homothetic patterns in integer grids.

title: Large Sieve and Quadratic Sets

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: If a set of positive integers occupies at most half the residue classes modulo every sufficiently large prime, must it either be substantially smaller than square-root size or lie entirely among the values of one rational quadratic polynomial at integers?

title: Covering Squares with Sumsets

category.name: number_theory
category.description: Properties of integers, prime numbers, Diophantine equations.

statement: Must a set whose pairwise sums contain every one of the first n positive squares have cardinality nearly n on the exponent scale?

title: Cubic Curves in F_p^2

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does every planar set over a large prime field with no three points on a line lie almost entirely on a curve of degree at most three?

title: Collinear Triples and Cubic Curves

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Must a planar point set with bounded line multiplicities and many pairs lying in collinear triples have a positive proportion of its points on one cubic curve?

title: Erdős-Szekeres with Visibility

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does every sufficiently large planar point set contain either many points on one line or a prescribed number of points with no other point blocking any connecting segment?

title: Collinear 4-tuples Force Collinear 5-tuples

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Must every large point set with a fixed positive quadratic number of collinear four-point subsets contain five collinear points?

title: Smooth Surfaces Intersecting 2-planes

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: In all sufficiently large dimensions, must every smooth local surface of codimension two meet some affine two-plane in at least five points?

title: No 5 Points on 2-plane in [N]^d

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: How large can a subset of a high-dimensional integer grid be if every affine two-plane contains at most four of its points?

title: Balanced Ham Sandwich Line

category.name: geometry
category.description: Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry, geometric structures.

statement: Does every finite planar point set admit a line through two of its points with at most one hundred points of imbalance between the two sides?

title: Comparable Elements in Integer Lattices

category.name: combinatorics
category.description: Counting problems, graph theory, discrete structures.

statement: Can one save a fixed power below the quadratic bound for sets of triples in which every pair has two coordinate differences of the same strict sign?

title: Stable Density on Subspaces
